meetings.title: BOCC - Budget Work Session #3 - June 1, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: At Budget Work Session #3 on June 1, 2023, Durham Technical Community College leaders presented their FY23-24 budget priorities, including living-wage janitorial contracts, workforce scholarships funded through Article 46 sales tax, in-house facilities positions, and faculty/staff recruitment and retention funds. Later in the session, commissioners and County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell debated whether to add a 30-minute Museum of Durham History presentation to the June 5 work session despite the City of Durham not yet considering the joint request. The board also reviewed opioid settlement fund governance and removed a $600,000 item from the budget add/delete list because three commissioners were not ready to support it.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0396: Durham Technical Community College and Economic Development Budget Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DTCC President J.B. Buxton, Chief Academic Officer Dr. Baddler, and Workforce Engagement Executive Director Jerry Jones presented five priorities in the County Manager's recommended budget: living wages (including a rebid housekeeping/janitorial contract meeting Durham County's living wage), key infrastructure positions such as an in-house plumber, economic and workforce development (Small Business Center and apprenticeship coordinators), faculty/staff recruitment and retention inducements, and student scholarships (Back-to-Work $700 non-credit grants, BULLS stipends, and Durham Tech Promise $500/semester grants). Buxton also noted plans to discuss repurposing Article 46 funds alongside a $50,000 private grant to cover textbooks and transportation for DPS high school students earning workforce credentials.

agenda_items.title: Museum of Durham History Budget Request and June 5 Work Session Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, commissioners discussed Commissioner Nida Allam's request to use an open 30-minute slot on June 5 for a presentation from the Museum of Durham History on facility expansion and staff salary increases. County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell and Budget Director Keith Lane noted she had moved the item to the June 13 Joint City-County meeting because the City had not yet received or processed the joint funding request. Commissioners ultimately agreed to allow a 30-minute informational presentation on June 5 while acknowledging that any joint funding decision would require coordination with the City.

agenda_items.title: Opioid Settlement Funds Process and Budget Add/Delete List Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff clarified that opioid settlement expenditures (now coordinated by Dwayne following Gudrun's departure) would be brought individually as specific strategies and initiatives are developed rather than bundled into the annual operating budget. Reviewing the add/delete list ahead of the June 5 wrap-up, commissioners confirmed that three members were not ready to proceed on a $600,000 item and agreed to remove it from the list, leaving a net general fund balance increase of $708,000.

disagreements.issue: Scheduling the Museum of Durham History Funding Presentation for the June 5 Budget Work Session
disagreements.summary: Commissioners and County Management disagreed on whether to place the Museum of Durham History's expansion and salary funding request on the June 5 final budget work session agenda before the City of Durham had acted on the joint request.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hear a 30-minute informational presentation from the Museum of Durham History at the June 5 work session so the full board can review the request before the July recess.
side_a_arguments: Not all commissioners have received the background information shared with the museum liaison, and the next regular work session after June is not until August due to the July break.
Joint City-County meetings do not include the full Board of County Commissioners, and Council Member Williams had already asked about it on the City side.
A 30-minute slot was open in the June 5 afternoon schedule.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer joint City-County funding requests like the Museum of Durham History to the June 13 Joint City-County meeting rather than placing unvetted joint asks on the June 5 budget wrap-up session.
side_b_arguments: Budget work sessions are intended for items the County will fund wholly and decide upon for the June 12 budget adoption, whereas the City budget office received the request late and was not considering it yet.
Making a County budget commitment or add/delete decision on June 5 without knowing the City's position would be premature, and any post-June 12 funding would require August fund balance action.
disagreements.resolution: Commissioners agreed to accommodate a strictly 30-minute informational presentation on June 5 while deferring any joint funding coordination to the June 13 Joint City-County meeting.

meetings.title: BOCC - Budget Work Session #2 - May 24, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: During Budget Work Session #2 on May 24, 2023, the board received an update on Durham's Refugee and Immigrant Affairs program, highlighting partner outreach, the MyDurham civic integration cohort, planned community resource and needs assessments, and delays in finalizing a City-County interlocal agreement. Commissioners also previewed Youth Home, Sheriff's Office Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT), and Justice Services' Familiar Faces and Stepping Up initiatives. Near the close of the session, staff outlined a late 3- to 3.5-cent tax rate increase request for the RTP Special Tax District, and commissioners debated agenda discipline for the remaining June 1 and June 5 budget work sessions as well as resident concerns regarding the Lebanon Fire District.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0081: Refugee and Immigrant Affairs Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Refugee and Immigrant Affairs Coordinator presented an overview of Durham's immigrant and refugee population—noting 14.8% speak languages other than English at home—along with over 100 partner meetings, the MyDurham civic integration program (200+ participants), and proposed resource mapping and needs assessment work. Commissioners discussed trust-building with immigrant communities, youth outreach through Durham Public Schools and Durham Tech, language access barriers, and following up on why the City-County interlocal agreement signed in October 2021 for the joint Office of Immigrant and Refugee Affairs had stalled at the City level.

agenda_items.title: Youth Home, Sheriff's Office Opioid/MAT Program, and Justice Services Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County staff introduced budget presentations covering the new Durham County Youth Home, the Sheriff's Office detention center opioid treatment and Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT) programs including a newly recommended medical director position, and Justice Services' Familiar Faces Initiative (FFI) and Stepping Up Initiative. (Subsequent middle remarks were truncated in the digest.)

agenda_items.title: RTP Special Tax District Rate Request, Lebanon Fire District, and June Budget Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and the County Attorney explained that a requested 3- to 3.5-cent property tax rate increase for the Research Triangle Park (RTP) special tax district arrived after the recommended budget was published and would be placed on the add/delete list for June 12 budget ordinance adoption, with clarification needed on its impact as RTP parcels convert from commercial to residential in 2024. Commissioners also debated the June 1 and June 5 work session agendas, with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs requesting information on full-time firefighter layoffs at the Lebanon Fire District and board-first review of Low-Income Homeowner Relief policy changes, while Commissioner Nimasheena Burns objected to adding late presentations or spilling into June 6.

disagreements.issue: Adding Late Presentations (Museum of Durham History, Lebanon Fire District) and Potentially Using June 6 for Budget Work Sessions
disagreements.summary: Commissioners differed over whether to add non-tax-rate or late-submitted presentations onto the June 1 and June 5 budget work sessions or extend deliberations to the reserved June 6 date.
disagreements.side_a_position: Add timely informational updates such as the Lebanon Fire District staffing transition and Museum of Durham History to upcoming work sessions, and ensure Low-Income Homeowner Relief policy changes come to the full BOCC first.
side_a_arguments: Residents in the Lebanon Fire District are alarmed about full-time firefighters being let go and potential impacts on response and homeowners insurance ratings.
The full BOCC does not attend Joint City-County meetings, so board members need direct briefings on policies they must approve.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep the June 1 and June 5 budget work sessions strictly focused on county budget decisions and honor the pre-scheduled calendar without spilling over to June 6.
side_b_arguments: The board already faces 7.5-hour budget work session days, and adding 30- to 45-minute late requests from external groups is unfair to budget staff and other presenters.
Budget dates have been on the calendar since the start of the year and should be honored rather than forcing staff and commissioners back on June 6.
disagreements.resolution: Staff noted Lebanon Fire District had no tax rate increase and would be placed on a regular work session after the budget, Low-Income Homeowner Relief policy updates would return to the full board without affecting the budget allocation, and the pre-set June 1 and June 5 schedule was maintained.

meetings.title: BOCC - May 22, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the May 22, 2023 Regular Session while Chair Brenda A. Howerton participated virtually. The board unanimously approved the April 24 minutes, issued an EMS Week proclamation, and conducted a collaborative reading of a joint Day of Remembrance resolution condemning youth and gun violence alongside Durham City Council and Durham Public Schools. Following discussion of a stakeholder-negotiated Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Release (TNVR) cat management proposal, commissioners unanimously directed the County Attorney to draft a formal Chapter 4 ordinance amendment resolution for a June 12 vote, and after a closed session unanimously authorized up to $285,000 in additional funding and condemnation authority for the Snow Hill Road pump station and force main replacement project.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Virtual Chair Notice, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs announced that Chair Brenda A. Howerton was attending virtually and that Jacobs would preside over the meeting. Clerk Monica Wallace read agenda announcements covering World Hunger Day Durham on June 4, the Durham Black Chamber of Commerce Enrich Bookkeeping Assistance Pilot Program, and the Sheriff's Office Start Talk podcast, followed by an animal shelter adoption reminder.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 24, 2023 Board Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved to approve the April 24, 2023 board minutes with no revisions noted. The motion was seconded and approved unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: EMS Week Proclamation, Military Appreciation, and Day of Remembrance Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read a proclamation declaring May 21–27, 2023 as EMS Week in Durham County, recognizing Chief Paramedic Mark Lockhart, regional fire and hospital partners, overdose outreach, and familiar-faces check-ins. After a military appreciation and Memorial Day appeal, commissioners led by Nimasheena Burns performed a round-robin reading of a joint Day of Remembrance resolution—crafted with Mayor O'Neal and DPS Board Chair Bettina Umstead—pledging action to reduce gun violence, support responsible gun ownership, and mobilize community volunteers for Durham youth.

agenda_items.title: Chapter 4 Animal Ordinance Amendment: Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Release (TNVR) Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle truncation in the digest, Commissioner Heidi Carter endorsed the March 21, 2023 stakeholder-negotiated draft allowing a volunteer-supported TNVR outdoor cat management program without requiring county budget funds. County Attorney Allen Andrews advised formalizing the amendment via a clean redlined resolution under County Ordinance 1-11 rather than adopting an unformatted draft on the spot. Carter then moved, seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam, to direct the County Attorney to prepare a Chapter 4 resolution based on the March 21, 2023 working group proposal for final action at the June 12, 2023 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney read the board's ballot appointment results for county boards and commissions, including William Young and Tia Rawlings (business representative on the Memorial Stadium Authority). Vice Chair Jacobs thanked the volunteers stepping forward to serve and noted no consent agenda items were pulled.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Snow Hill Road Pump Station / Force Main Replacement Authorization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) to instruct staff on real property acquisition negotiations and employment contract compensation terms. Upon returning to open session at 03:48:51, commissioners unanimously approved a motion authorizing up to $285,000 in additional funding for the Snow Hill Road pump station and force main replacement project and directing staff to exercise all powers, including condemnation, to acquire necessary parcels before adjourning.

meetings.title: BOCC - Budget Work Session #1 - May 16, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: At Budget Work Session #1 on May 16, 2023, budget staff reviewed the fiscal framework behind the County Manager's FY23-24 recommended budget, highlighting $35.8 million in natural revenue growth, strong sales tax and Medicaid hold harmless gains, a 3-cent total property tax rate increase (split evenly between general fund operations and 2022 GO Bond capital financing), and $15 million in MAG study and merit pay raises. Staff also noted $2.5 million in operational reductions from historical unspent departmental funds and previewed upcoming property revaluation effects and a pending Research Triangle Foundation tax rate request. In the afternoon portion, staff updated commissioners on the BULLS life sciences workforce initiative, one-time funding priorities including a homeless day center RFP and water/sewer infrastructure needs, and the Interise MWBE training program.

agenda_items.title: FY23-24 Budget Revenue Outlook, Property Tax Rate, Compensation, and Revaluation Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget staff presented the macroeconomic and revenue picture for the FY23-24 recommended budget, reporting $35.8 million in natural general fund revenue growth led by $21.8 million in total new sales tax revenue ($13.4M general fund, $8.4M capital financing) and $12 million in Medicaid hold harmless funds. To fund the 7% MAG study compensation increase ($10.5M), 3–4% merit increases ($4.5M), full Durham Public Schools funding, and nearly $2 million in added DTCC support ($2.4M total in Article 46 scholarships), the budget pairs $2.5 million in departmental operational reallocations with a 3-cent property tax increase (1.5 cents general fund and 1.5 cents 2022 GO Bond debt service). Staff also previewed the upcoming property revaluation—projecting a revenue-neutral rate in the high 50s or 60s—and noted a late RTP tax district request scheduled for May 24.

agenda_items.title: BULLS Workforce Initiative, One-Time Funding Proposals, and Interise MWBE Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, staff and Assistant County Manager Tammy Hall briefed the board on the BULLS workforce pipeline as cohorts 4 and 5 prepared to graduate, noting an $800,000 Made in Durham grant for nonprofit success coaches, $250,000 in annual county stipends, plans for DPS teacher externships, independent program evaluation, and adding a second industry pathway alongside biopharma. Commissioners praised the program while pressing for earlier outreach to enrolled DPS high school students and stronger post-graduation job interview placement. Staff also discussed one-time funding priorities—such as a homeless day center RFP, a small business entrepreneurship fund, and nearly $100 million in water/sewer needs—and reported progress on the 13-week Interise MWBE Evolution training program.

meetings.title: County Manager's Recommended Fiscal Year 23-24 Budget Presentation
meetings.executive_summary: On May 11, 2023, County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell formally presented the FY23-24 Recommended Budget to the Board of County Commissioners pursuant to N.C.G.S. 159-12. Highlighting $36 million in natural revenue growth outpaced by $38 million in core priority increases, Sowell proposed a 3-cent property tax rate increase (1.5 cents general fund, 1.5 cents capital financing) to fund a 7% MAG compensation study adjustment plus 3%–4% merit raises for county employees while limiting new position growth. Education remained the largest investment at over $207 million—fully funding Durham Public Schools' request at $188 million, raising DTCC support by nearly $2 million, and adding over $1 million for Durham Pre-K—alongside new investments in detention center medical/opioid care, the Youth Home, a new Office of Engagement, and 2024 election readiness.

agenda_items.title: Manager's Strategic Vision, Organizational Restructure, and Position Restraint
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell opened her FY23-24 budget address under N.C.G.S. 159-12 by announcing a reimagining of Durham County's strategic plan as a measurable framework for all policy and budget choices. She described an internal leadership reorganization establishing deputy and assistant county manager portfolios and explained her intentional decision to limit new FTE additions while existing vacancies remain high.

agenda_items.title: Revenue Outlook, 3-Cent Tax Rate Recommendation, and Employee Compensation (MAG Study)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sowell reported $36 million in natural revenue growth from property tax, sales tax, Medicaid hold harmless funds, occupancy tax, and fund balance, contrasted with $38 million in core priority cost increases. To retain county staff amid inflation and regional competition, the budget implements the Management Advisory Group (MAG) compensation study recommendation of a 7% across-the-board increase plus 3%–4% pay-for-performance merit raises (10%–11% maximum), supported by a recommended 3-cent property tax rate increase split between 1.5 cents for capital financing and 1.5 cents for general fund operations.

agenda_items.title: Education Funding: Durham Public Schools ($188M), DTCC (+20%), and Universal Pre-K
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Recommending over $207 million across education partners, Sowell proposed fully funding Durham Public Schools' request at $188 million (33% of the general fund, including a $10.8 million current expense increase lifting per-pupil funding by $289 to $4,650 per student, plus ~$58 million in indirect county support). The budget also increases Durham Tech funding by nearly $2 million (20%, including $520,000 more for $2.4 million total in Durham Student Scholarships and school-to-work pipeline roles) and adds over $1 million to expand Durham Pre-K by up to 100 children.

agenda_items.title: Community Safety, Veterans Services, Engagement Office, Elections, and Adoption Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sowell detailed targeted investments including $532,000 for second-year food security grants, an additional Veteran Services Officer, a dedicated detention center medical director for the Sheriff's Office opioid/MAT program, CJRC psychiatric services and the Familiar Faces Initiative, opening the new Youth Home and assessment center, and expanded JCPC juvenile crime prevention grants. New administrative positions include an Office of Engagement (manager and data analyst), two Board of Elections positions for the new elections warehouse ahead of 2024, an IS&T broadband manager, and an ERP financial business analyst, leading into work sessions (May 16–June 5), a May 22 public hearing, and June 12 adoption.

meetings.title: BOCC - May 8, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the May 8, 2023 Regular Session with a moment of silence for victims of gun violence in Texas, followed by announcements including Fidelity Investments' extended May 15 scholarship deadline for Durham students. The board unanimously (5-0) approved the April 10 regular session minutes and adopted proclamations for Resilient and Thriving Communities Week (23-0308) and Older Americans Month (23-0309). Later, the board held a public hearing with no speakers on updated water and sewer System Development Fees (to be incorporated into the upcoming budget) and received the Management Advisory Group (MAG) compensation study and proposed pay plan establishing a $19.22/hour living wage floor and 7% across-the-board pay adjustment.

agenda_items.title: Moment of Silence, Agenda Announcements, and Fidelity Scholars Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton led a moment of silence for children and residents killed in Texas before Clerk Monica Wallace read announcements on free COVID-19 home test kits, the June 1 homestead property tax relief deadline, the end of pandemic SNAP/EBT emergency allotments, a library bookmark contest, and foster care recruitment. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns added an announcement that Fidelity Investments extended its May 15 application deadline for its $250 million last-dollar scholarship program for African American and Hispanic students in Durham and four other NC cities.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 10, 2023 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no edits requested, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously voted 5-0 by voice vote to approve the April 10, 2023 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: Resilient and Thriving Communities Week (23-0308) and Older Americans Month (23-0309)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns read resolution 23-0308 proclaiming April 29–May 6, 2023 as Resilient and Thriving Communities Week, accepted by Public Health Adverse Childhood Experiences and Resilience Coordinator Jess Bosquette, with commissioners highlighting the Surgeon General's advisory on youth loneliness and upcoming joint school board mental health discussions. Commissioner Heidi Carter then read proclamation 23-0309 recognizing May 2023 as Older Americans Month in coordination with the Department of Social Services.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Updated Water and Sewer System Development Fees (SDF)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, rate consultants and staff presented the five-year update to Durham County's System Development Fees, noting the county had been dramatically undercharging relative to calculated full-cost-recovery fees needed to support capital projects. Chair Howerton opened and closed the public hearing with no speakers signed up in person or on Zoom, and staff confirmed no separate vote was needed as the revised fees would be included in the upcoming budget adoption.

agenda_items.title: Other Business: Management Advisory Group (MAG) Compensation Study and Proposed Pay Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief HR Officer Kathy Everett-Perry introduced MAG consultant Russell Campbell, who presented the compensation study and pay plan affecting 1,876 county employees, recommending movement to the 75th market percentile, a 7% general salary increase, pay-for-performance adjustments, and a $19.22/hour living wage floor indexed annually to the Consumer Price Index. Commissioners welcomed the $19.22 living wage and clear compensation policies, noted existing hard-to-fill sign-on bonuses for detention officers, EMS technicians, and youth home counselors, and deferred deeper discussion to the upcoming budget work sessions.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 10, 2023 Regular Session Minutes
votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not identified by name in the audio transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: No edits or comments were offered on the April 10, 2023 regular session minutes. The motion was moved, seconded, and passed 5-0 by voice vote.

meetings.title: BOCC - April 24, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 24, 2023 Regular Session, Chair Brenda A. Howerton welcomed new Department of Social Services Director Maggie Cveticanin and the board approved the April 3 work session minutes (5-0) and proclaimed April 30 as National Therapy Animal Day. Commissioners unanimously approved (5-0) the consent agenda—including 24 ARPA nonprofit contracts out of the $10.3 million allocation—while briefly pulling item 23-0277 so Commissioner Heidi Carter could highlight the Community Child Protection Team's preventable safe-sleep recommendations. The board also reviewed an Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) and trauma-informed policy presentation and announced multiple board and commission ballot appointments while deferring a Juvenile Crime Prevention Council citizen seat for additional applicants.

agenda_items.title: Community Announcements and Introduction of New DSS Director
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Wallace read community announcements including Public Health COVID-19 vaccine walk-in hours, the April 26 Local Reentry Council Resource Fair, the Durham Dementia Community Event, the Carolina Flyers home opener, and open 2023-24 Durham Pre-K applications. Chair Brenda A. Howerton also welcomed new Department of Social Services (DSS) Director Maggie Cveticanin during her second week on the job.

agenda_items.title: Approval of April 3, 2023 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no edits or corrections proposed, the board moved, seconded, and approved the April 3, 2023 work session minutes by a 5-0 voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item: National Therapy Animal Day Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring April 30, 2023 as National Therapy Animal Day in Durham County, accepted by a Pet Partners therapy animal volunteer, with commissioners praising therapy animals' stress-relief benefits for students and youth.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (23-0130 to 23-0300), Pulled Item 23-0277, and ARPA Nonprofit Contracts Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved all consent agenda items except 23-0277 on a 5-0 vote, allowing Commissioner Heidi Carter to highlight the Community Child Protection Team's report on preventable infant deaths and urge administrative review of safe-sleep campaign recommendations ahead of the budget. Later at 02:27:13, County Manager Dr. Sowell highlighted that the consent agenda included 24 nonprofit contracts from the $10.3 million ARPA allocation across seven focus areas and noted staff were updating a public county webpage tracking funded outside organizations.

agenda_items.title: Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs), Trauma-Informed Policy, and Environmental Justice Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle gap in the digest, commissioners responded to a presentation from Jess Bosquette and Rod on adverse childhood experiences, cultural and climate trauma, and racial equity. Commissioners urged translating the framework into actionable budget and policy measures—including trauma-informed and racial-equity budget screening, youth programs, universal basic income concepts, and monitoring PFAS environmental impacts—while staff noted a formal resolution would return in coming weeks.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney announced ballot appointments to the Durham County Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees (Whitney Stanley and Charles Cooperberg), Duke Regional Medical Staff (Philip Bong), Lincoln Community Health Center (Federico Manion), Duke Regional Physicians (Michelle L. Al-Hegelan), and the Historic Preservation Commission (Kenneth Webb). Because no candidate received a board majority for a Juvenile Crime Prevention Council citizen seat, the board deferred that appointment to the following month to gather more applicants.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not identified by name in the audio transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: No edits or corrections were raised for the April 3, 2023 work session minutes. A motion and second were made, and the board passed the minutes 5-0 by voice vote.

meetings.title: Durham City-County Joint Meeting for April 11, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Durham County Commissioners and City of Durham leaders convened for the April 11, 2023 Joint City-County Meeting, with Commissioner Wendy Jacobs joining virtually while traveling. Durham Crisis Response Center Executive Director Damien Talley provided a pre-opening update on the Family Justice Center (set to open April 24, 2023) and its Spanish-language and immigrant victim services. Leaders also strategized on convening a rapid community 'roll call' of nonprofits to coordinate summer youth camp capacity and promote an April 22 joint job fair, and the Mayor presented four shovel-ready affordable housing developments seeking County matching gap funds alongside $10 million committed by the City.

agenda_items.title: Introductions and Family Justice Center / Durham Crisis Response Center Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Wanda Page, City Attorney Kimberly Rehberg, Commissioner Nida Allam, Durham Crisis Response Center Executive Director Damien Talley, and County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell opened with introductions, noting Commissioner Wendy Jacobs participated via Zoom while traveling. Talley updated officials on the Family Justice Center's April 24, 2023 grand opening, highlighting Legal Aid and Sheriff's Office co-location, 15 Latinx women and children sheltered via the Spanish crisis line, and 165 individuals served by immigrant services.

agenda_items.title: Summer Youth Programming Roll Call of Nonprofits and Joint Job Fair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Officials discussed addressing summer programming gaps for older youth beyond the roughly 5,000 younger students reached by Durham Public Schools summer programs. Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Mayor/board colleagues supported convening a rapid 'roll call' of local nonprofits (such as Durham Children's Initiative, YMCA, Museum of Life and Science, Boys & Girls Club, and Salvation Army) to inventory camp seats, scholarships, and donated resources without duplicating existing fundraising, alongside a joint City-County-DPS job fair on April 22.

agenda_items.title: Item #4: Affordable Housing Partnerships — Four Shovel-Ready City RFP Priority Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Mayor outlined four shovel-ready affordable housing developments from the City's RFP round that lacked full gap financing—noting the City allocated $10 million and hoped the County would match each project (each needing just under $5 million from the City): East Geer Street (~84 units at 30%–80% AMI), the Durham Tech Briggs Avenue initiative (120+ units prioritizing DTCC students), Dearborn Drive Multifamily (~200 units with 100 at 60% AMI plus permanent space for the VFW), and Sandy Ridge Phase 2. Leaders thanked City and County housing staff (Bertha and Claudia) and noted the next joint meeting would be June 13.

meetings.title: BOCC - April 10, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Opening the April 10, 2023 Regular Session after closed session, the board unanimously authorized staff to sign the Supplemental Agreement for Additional Funds (SAAF) and five National Opioid Settlement participation agreements (CVS, Walgreens, Walmart, Allergan, and Teva) and formally exited closed session. Commissioners approved the March 27 minutes (5-0), issued proclamations for Second Chance Month and National County Government Month, and honored Patrick Hannah for his 2015–2023 service and chairmanship on the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority board. The board then unanimously approved a 43-item consent agenda and, following a public hearing with no speakers, voted 5-0 to adopt the revised County Stormwater Ordinance (Item 22-0216) incentivizing Low Impact Development to meet May 1 state watershed deadlines.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Action: National Opioid Settlement (SAAF and Five Participation Agreements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Allen Andrews reported that in closed session the board agreed to participate in the Supplemental Agreement for Additional Funds (SAAF) and five national opioid litigation agreements with CVS, Walgreens, Walmart, Allergan, and Teva. In open session, commissioners unanimously approved a motion (seconded by Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs) authorizing staff as signatory and adopting the conforming resolution, followed by a formal motion to exit closed session.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Approval of March 27, 2023 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff read announcements on county summer/management internships and fellowships, Welcome Babies breastfeeding support classes, and Partnership for a Healthy Durham's 2022 Community Health Assessment presentation. After Commissioner Nida Allam reminded the chair to take up the minutes, the board unanimously voted 5-0 to approve the March 27, 2023 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions: Second Chance Month, Patrick Hannah (RDU), and County Government Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nida Allam read a proclamation declaring April 2023 as Second Chance Month, accepted by Criminal Justice Resource Center Assistant Director Rashana Parker (with Director Gudrun Parmer), noting more than 400 residents returning from prison and nearly 6,600 jail entries annually alongside an April calendar of reentry events. Later, the board presented a resolution honoring Patrick Hannah for his 2015–2023 service and chairmanship on the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority board, and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring April 2023 as National County Government Month.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (43 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presented the 43-item consent agenda and asked if any commissioner wished to pull an item for separate discussion. Hearing no requests, the board moved, seconded (by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns), and unanimously approved all 43 consent items.

agenda_items.title: Item 22-0216: Public Hearing and Adoption of Revised County Stormwater Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stormwater and Erosion Control Division Manager Ryan Eaves and Stormwater Manager McKenzie Bradshaw presented the revised County Stormwater Ordinance, reorganizing rules for clarity and fulfilling state Neuse/Falls/Jordan watershed management requirements ahead of a May 1 deadline. Answering Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, Eaves explained the update incentivizes Low Impact Development (LID) and green infrastructure by exempting qualifying low-impact designs from additional stormwater control measure calculations; after a public hearing with no speakers, the board voted 5-0 to adopt the ordinance.

votes.discussion_detail: After Commissioner Nida Allam reminded the board that the minutes had been skipped before proclamations, the board called for any edits to the March 27, 2023 regular meeting minutes, moved, seconded, and passed them 5-0 by voice vote.

meetings.title: BOCC - Work Session for April 3, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the April 3, 2023 Board of County Commissioners work session, which opened with public comments urging $1.875 million in ARPA funding for an extremely low-income rental assistance guaranteed income pilot and updating the Board on City Council review of the Simplifying Codes for Affordable Development (SCAD) text amendments. Commissioners reviewed 19 consent agenda items—highlighting $473,659 in ARPA water assistance for DSS, $875,000 in LOBs contingency for the 500 East Main Street parking deck, $145,520 for detention center security upgrades, and $300,800 for provider selection at the 300 East Main Street childcare center—and received a Criminal Justice Resource Center detention services presentation noting that 47% of jail bookings are referred to mental health services. The Board suspended the rules to approve two Cooperative Extension general fund balance appropriations and food-security contracts: $28,257.57 with Farmer Foodshare for the Double Bucks program (5-0) and $503,795.56 with the Interfaith Food Shuttle (4-0). Following a closed session on personnel matters, the Board voted 4-0 in open session to appoint Theresa Harrison as Interim Tax Administrator effective immediately.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Citizens' Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the public charge and opened 30 minutes of citizens' comments. James of Aura (Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit) urged the Board to allocate $1.875 million in remaining ARPA funds for a $600-per-month rental assistance guaranteed income pilot for extremely low-income renters facing eviction. James Chavis criticized unreturned follow-up from July 2022, Bob Chapman updated the Board that City Council requested an item-by-item Planning Department analysis of SCAD text amendments ahead of a May 1 public hearing before coming to the BOCC, and a fourth speaker thanked the Board for supporting equity framework work, My Brother's Keeper, and Community Intervention and Support Services.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (DSS Water Assistance, 500 E. Main Parking Deck, Jail Security, and 300 E. Main Childcare)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell introduced the 19-item consent agenda, including Item 23-0094 (23BCC0082 recognizing $473,659 in federal ARPA Low-Income Household Water Assistance funds for DSS), Item 23-0192 (23CPA0020 appropriating $875,000 in future taxable LOBs for the 500 East Main Street parking deck contingency with ZOM Living up to $32,701,100), Item 23-0193 ($145,520 Sheriff's Office contract with JNA Engineering LLC for detention center electric security replacement), and Item 23-0197 (23BCC0077 appropriating $300,800 for a contract with Child Care Services Association for the 300 East Main Street pre-K/childcare center). Commissioners Wendy Jacobs and Chair Brenda A. Howerton highlighted the county's second major downtown childcare investment, noting local childcare deserts and support for low-income downtown workers.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0173: Criminal Justice Resource Center (CJRC) Detention Services Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CJRC staff and Kelly Aknazic briefed the Board on intake screening, substance use disorder medication verification, discharge planning, and mental health referrals inside the detention center, reporting that 47% of booked individuals were referred to mental health services last year. Staff also reviewed Medicaid sign-ups, MacArthur Foundation-supported risk assessment work, jail bed days saved, and daily jail operating costs rising from $98.73 to $199.50 in FY21. Commissioners asked about tracking mental-health-related recidivism and pursuing outside philanthropic grants such as MacKenzie Scott's open call.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0225: Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0083 (Farmer Foodshare Double Bucks Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Food Security Coordinator Mary Oxendine and Cooperative Extension presented Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0083 to appropriate $28,257.57 in general fund balance for a contract with Farmer Foodshare supporting the Durham County Double Bucks program. After brief commissioner questions, the Board voted 4-0 to suspend the rules and then voted 5-0 to approve the budget amendment and contract.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0227: Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0080 (Interfaith Food Shuttle Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0080 to appropriate $503,795.56 in general fund balance and approve a contract with the Interfaith Food Shuttle to provide food to Durham County residents seeking food assistance. One commissioner remarked that it felt as though the Board was whittling down its fund balance, and staff assured the Board that the county remained in a solid fiscal position. The Board voted 4-0 to suspend the rules and 4-0 to approve the appropriation and contract.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Appointment of Interim Tax Administrator
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a commissioner request to introduce new County Manager team members at a future meeting, the Board voted to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider personnel qualifications and appointment. Returning to open session at 06:27:27, the Board voted 4-0 to appoint Theresa Harrison as Interim Tax Administrator effective immediately.

votes.notes: Chair announced 4-0; individual commissioner absences/names were not called aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Following questions on the Cooperative Extension Double Bucks request, Chair Brenda A. Howerton entertained a motion to suspend the rules so the Board could vote at the work session. The motion was seconded and passed 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.notes: Chair initially misread the figure as $28 million before reading the exact $28,257.57 amount.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Item 23-0227 (Interfaith Food Shuttle)
votes.notes: Chair announced 4-0; individual commissioner absences/names were not called aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff asked the Board to suspend the rules to act on Item 23-0227 at the work session. The motion was moved, seconded, and approved 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0227: Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0080 ($503,795.56 for Interfaith Food Shuttle Contract)
votes.notes: Chair announced 4-0; which single commissioner was absent/not voting was not stated.
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to approve Budget Ordinance Amendment 23BCC0080 appropriating $503,795.56 of general fund balance and approving a contract with Interfaith Food Shuttle for food assistance. During discussion, a member raised concern about drawing down fund balance, and staff affirmed the county remained in a solid position; the motion passed 4-0 by voice vote.

votes.notes: Exact numerical tally was not announced aloud on the closed-session motion.

votes.item_title: Appointment of Theresa Harrison as Interim Tax Administrator
votes.notes: Chair announced 4-0; which single commissioner was absent/not voting was not stated.

meetings.title: BOCC - March 27, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the March 27, 2023 regular session, opening with her annual State of the County Address reviewing the $793.56 million FY2023 budget, unchanged $0.7222 tax rate, $177.15 million Durham Public Schools funding, Pre-K and Durham Tech investments, economic development such as Kempower's 360+ jobs, and the upcoming FY2024 budget calendar. Commissioners also reviewed a resolution supporting universal no-cost school meals in the state budget and unanimously approved five consent agenda items (5-0 for the main consent slate and 5-0 for the pulled Environmental Affairs Board report, Item 23-0195, after public comment). During boards and commissions appointments, Commissioner Nida Allam moved to extend the application period for the Raleigh-Durham (RDU) Airport Authority Board unless candidates achieved majority support on the ballot, which passed 4-1; one RDU vacancy was filled by ballot while the second seat was held open for re-advertisement. After a closed session on personnel and litigation, the Board returned to open session and voted 5-0 to approve a $170,000 starting salary for new DSS Director Maggie Cveticanin.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Public Charge, and Pledge of Allegiance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the March 27, 2023 Board of County Commissioners regular session to order and read the public charge. She asked Commissioner Nida Allam to lead the Pledge of Allegiance.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0210: 2023 State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton delivered the 2023 State of the County Address, recognizing fellow commissioners, retired department heads Ben Rose and Willie Darby, late County Attorney Lowell Siler, and award-winning departments including Budget, Elections, Public Health, EMS, and Social Services. She highlighted the Hayti Reborn interlocal agreement, maternal health initiatives, Kempower's 360+ new jobs, and the $793,563,860 FY2023 budget ($0.7222 tax rate, $177.15 million for DPS, $6.4 million for Pre-K, and $9.74 million for Durham Tech). Chair Howerton closed by noting that the Manager's recommended FY2024 budget would be presented on May 8 with a public hearing on May 22.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Universal No-Cost School Meals in the State Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed a March 27 resolution urging the North Carolina General Assembly to fund universal free breakfast and lunch for all public school students in the state budget. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and commissioners supported sharing the signed resolution with the local legislative delegation and the Durham Public Schools Board of Education, and Clerk Monica Wallace confirmed it would be circulated for signatures and emailed out the next morning.

meetings.title: BOCC - March 13, 2023 - Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the March 13, 2023 regular session, which approved the February 27, 2023 regular session minutes and presented ceremonial recognitions for Year of the Trail, Women's History Month, and retiring 4th District U.S. Congressman David E. Price. Following a public hearing discussion on a general rezoning along Falls/Jordan from Residential Rural to Commercial General—where one commissioner voiced reservations about the breadth of the Commercial General district under state general-rezoning rules—the Board voted to adopt the rezoning ordinance and passed the statutory consistency statement 5-0. Under Item 23-0198, the Board held a public hearing with no speakers and voted 5-0 to adopt the final approving resolution for up to $235 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A and 2023B) to convert prior short-term draw financing into long-term fixed-rate debt. The meeting concluded with Item 23-0143, an informational Department of Social Services briefing on updated placement protocols for medically complex children aimed at avoiding needless institutionalization.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and asked for the Pledge of Allegiance. Clerk Monica Wallace read community announcements covering walk-in COVID-19 vaccination hours, Durham Pre-K enrollment events, a March 20 public input session on Durham County's $11.6 million in National Opioid Settlement funds over 18 years, the Emily K Center College Expo, and AARP Tax-Aide. The Board then voted to approve the February 27, 2023 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Year of the Trail, Resolution Honoring Congressman David E. Price, and Women's History Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board presented Item 23-0183 proclaiming Year of the Trail and promoting local Creek Week and trail events, followed by Item 23-0189 honoring the retirement of U.S. Representative David E. Price for his decades of service in Congress, appropriations leadership, and advocacy for RTP and Durham's life sciences sector. Congressman Price and commissioners exchanged remarks reflecting on his constituent engagement, and the Board later read a Women's History Month recognition.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: General Rezoning on Falls/Jordan (Residential Rural to Commercial General)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During public hearing deliberation on a general rezoning on Falls/Jordan from Residential Rural to Commercial General, staff clarified that state statute prohibits attaching use conditions to a general rezoning and explained that unlike a City annexation (which triggers City Code cost-benefit and service-operation analyses), a county general rezoning only changes the zoning district. A commissioner expressed unease over how broad the Commercial General district is while still indicating support. The Board adopted the rezoning ordinance and passed the N.C.G.S. 160D-605 consistency statement 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0198: Public Hearing and Final Resolution for Not-to-Exceed $235 Million Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A and 2023B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff presented the final resolution for up to $235 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A and 2023B), continuing the financing calendar initiated on February 27 to convert draw-program debt into long-term fixed-rate financing via a supplemental installment contract amendment. After voting to open and close the public hearing with no speakers signed up, the Board voted 5-0 to adopt the final approving resolution.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS staff presented updated placement protocols and guidelines intended to ensure children with medically complex needs are cared for in home settings rather than needlessly institutionalized. Commissioners discussed state DHHS policy constraints, Alliance Health coordination for therapeutic needs, hospital referral workflows, and DSS staff sacrifices during COVID-19.

meetings.title: BOCC - Work Session for March 6, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the March 6, 2023 Board of County Commissioners work session, enforcing strict time limits to move through a packed agenda. After hearing citizen comment from Sharon Hunter regarding a court restitution refund, the Board reviewed consent agenda items covering Public Health grants, a $250,000 general fund balance appropriation for out-of-county Youth Home placements, a $141,462 Sheriff's Office detention center body scanner, IT contracts, Criminal Justice Resource Center (CJRC) local reentry grants, and Phase 2 of the Alston Glenn farm conservation easement. Later in the session, commissioners questioned City Transportation and GoDurham staff on transit corridor budgets, bus stop maintenance accountability, fare-free transit continuity, and integrating affordable housing at Durham Station. The meeting concluded with discussions on a proposed $10 million County ARPA contribution toward four joint affordable housing projects, a Permanent Supportive Housing campus concept, and a request for an emergency management briefing on freight rail safety.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Citizens' Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the work session, read the public charge, and asked commissioners and presenters to adhere to a strict three-minute question limit due to the packed agenda. Resident Sharon Hunter spoke during public comment regarding dismissed 2020 criminal charges involving her son's mental health status and difficulties obtaining a court restitution refund from bookkeeping.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Public Health, Youth Home, Sheriff's Office, IT, CJRC, and Farmland Preservation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell walked through consent agenda items including five Public Health budget amendments (23-0044, 23-0045, 23-0046, 23-0048, and 23-0144), a $250,000 appropriation for Durham Youth Home out-of-county placements (23-0098), a $141,462 detention center body scanner contract with Tech 84 Inc., a $300,000 roofing project reduction (23-0109), the 2022 BPAC annual report (23-0113), IT contracts (Westaff, Info-Tech, Carahsoft, and SHI Microsoft licensing), CJRC Local Reentry Council grants (23-0148 and 23-0151, part of a $600,000+ City-County ARPA reentry housing collaboration), and a $142,500 transfer for Phase 2 of the Alston Glenn farm conservation easement (23-0156). Commissioners asked follow-up questions on communicable disease reporting, the mobile unit plan, Youth Home placement frustration, and quarterly CJRC data reports.

agenda_items.title: City Transportation and GoDurham Transit Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Transportation and GoDurham transit staff answered commissioner questions regarding budgets for the Fayetteville and Holloway transit corridors, the absence of a standalone city transit plan equivalent to the County Transit Plan (relying instead on the CIP, Bike+Walk plan, and GoTriangle's Short-Range Transit Plan update), and why affordable housing was not included in the current Durham Station renovation design. Staff also explained new operator contract tiers for bus stop trash and shelter maintenance, noted City Council commitment to fare-free bus service pending the City Manager's budget, and discussed tracking legacy versus transit-tax expansion metrics.

agenda_items.title: Joint City-County Affordable Housing ARPA Investment, Permanent Supportive Housing Campus, and Freight Rail Safety Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed county housing partnerships, emergency rental assistance, and a proposal for the County to contribute $10 million in federal/ARPA funds alongside the City so four affordable housing projects could move forward without funding shortfalls. Gudrun Parmer also previewed a Permanent Supportive Housing campus concept modeled on Wake County and Charlotte (noting Charlotte data showing average emergency room bills dropping from $40,000 to $12,000 for housed residents) to gauge Board interest ahead of late March or April. Before concluding, a commissioner requested a future emergency management briefing on Durham's safety plan for freight rail traffic following a second Norfolk Southern accident.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Annual Budget Retreat Day 2 - March 1, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened Day 2 of the Board of County Commissioners Annual Budget Retreat on March 1, 2023, with Commissioner Nida Allam participating remotely via Zoom. HR and Budget staff reviewed the county's living wage policy and recommended a 9% increase from $16.90 to $18.40 per hour while warning against jumping to $23–$24 per hour or immediately extending the floor to all Durham Public Schools (DPS) employees due to salary compression and property tax pressures alongside the recently passed school bond. DSS staff then presented a SWOT analysis and FY23 utilization review of the Longtime Homeowners Relief Fund—projecting roughly $330,000 in spending out of its $1.25 million budget and floating a right-sized FY24 split—before commissioners closed the retreat by outlining FY24 budget priorities including DPS pay parity, a Durham Tech workforce pipeline, City-County housing and service-overlap coordination, reproductive care, immigrant services, Hayti Reborn, transit tax needs, and Veteran Services outreach.

agenda_items.title: Day 2 Opening and Agenda Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton welcomed commissioners to Day 2 of the budget retreat and acknowledged Commissioner Nida Allam joining via Zoom. County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell outlined the half-day agenda covering living wage options, the Longtime Homeowners Relief Fund, a Board of Elections space update, and Board budget priority discussions.

agenda_items.title: Living Wage Policy Update and DPS Employee Compensation Tradeoffs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR and Budget staff presented on the county's living wage policy (currently 7.5% above federal poverty guidelines, or $32,250 annually) and recommended raising the hourly floor by 9% from $16.90 to $18.40 without requesting a formal vote at the retreat. Staff cautioned that $23–$24 per hour proposals or extending the county wage floor to all DPS employees would impose exorbitant costs and pay compression alongside DPS's $10.8 million request and upcoming debt service from the historic school bond (potentially up to a 2.5-cent tax impact). Commissioners asked about mandatory overtime in vacant departments and total compensation equity including childcare and education benefits.

agenda_items.title: Longtime Homeowners Relief Fund (LTHP) Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS staff presented a SWOT analysis identifying foreclosure and gentrification as key threats and reported FY23 spending of approximately $302,000 (projected ~$330,000 with 20–25 pending applications) out of the $1.25 million joint budget ($750,000 County and $500,000 City via ILA), which also funded three administrative support positions. Staff noted discussions with the DSS board about potentially right-sizing the FY24 budget (such as halving allocations to $325,000 County and $250,000 City) while preserving room for program growth.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner FY24 Budget Priorities and Veteran Services Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners articulated individual budget priorities, including support for the Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit's rental assistance proposal, a farm/supportive housing campus, and maximizing fund balance and grants. Commissioner Nida Allam advocated for extending the $18.40 wage increase to DPS staff, creating a Durham Tech workforce pipeline for EMS/public health/fire marshal vacancies, funding City-managed joint housing projects, studying City-County service overlap, creating a reproductive care fund, reviewing immigrant/refugee Welcome Center needs, and praising the new grant coordinator role. Other commissioners lifted up Hayti Reborn, mental health, the 2050 transportation plan's 1.5-cent transit sales tax, and Veteran Services Director Lois urged the Board to fund staffing and a $35,000 outreach vehicle.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners - Annual Budget Retreat Day 1 - February 28, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: On Day 1 of the Board of County Commissioners Annual Budget Retreat on February 28, 2023, County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell framed the FY23–24 budget development process and asked commissioners to narrow their November policy retreat priorities to their top three goals. Finance and Budget staff briefed the Board on the county's interest rate swap (maturing March 1, 2031, retained per financial advisor analysis to help offset over $60 million in annual debt service), 13 consecutive years of exceeding 100% of budgeted revenues, and peer-county financial comparisons against Mecklenburg, Wake, Guilford, Forsyth, and Orange counties. The Board also reviewed Public Health and maternal health funding distinctions between one-time ARPA items and recurring costs—with a request for inclusive outreach language and follow-up on a United Way-facilitated doula consortium—before holding an extensive briefing on the new Youth Home and Juvenile Assessment Center. Youth Home leadership presented a three-tier phased bed opening plan (16–36 beds) and warned of a 52% to 57% staffing vacancy rate, calling for a $50,000–$52,000 starting salary and overtime reforms ahead of opening.

agenda_items.title: Budget Retreat Day 1 Framing and Priority Narrowing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell outlined the two-day retreat agenda, noting Day 1 financial updates, ARPA reviews, and a Youth Home briefing, followed by Day 2 discussions on living wage ($23–$24/hour proposals alongside compensation study work), the Longtime Homeowners Relief Fund, and relocating the Board of Elections to the former Shops at Hope Valley. She asked commissioners to narrow their November policy retreat list down to three top priorities to guide FY24 budget drafting.

agenda_items.title: Financial Highlights, Interest Rate Swap Analysis, and Peer County Comparisons
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff reported that despite Federal Reserve interest rate volatility, financial advisors determined Durham County should remain in its interest rate swap through its March 1, 2031 maturity, using swap fund balance to help cover over $60 million in annual debt service and stabilize the property tax rate. Staff also noted 13 straight years of collecting over 100% of budgeted revenues (109.8% revenues vs. 92.86% expenditures in FY21) and compared Durham's budget execution and fund balance growth against peer North Carolina counties, with a commissioner requesting bond-rating columns be added.

agenda_items.title: Public Health, ARPA Eligibility, and Maternal Health Outreach
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff discussed aligning one-time Public Health items with ARPA eligibility while evaluating recurring costs through the regular budget process. Commissioners inquired about a follow-up from community doula organizations and a United Way-facilitated doula consortium, and requested that county maternal health materials use inclusive language recognizing non-binary and trans birthing people.

agenda_items.title: Youth Home and Juvenile Assessment Center Phased Budget and Staffing Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Angela Nunn and Gudrun Parmer presented a phased operating model for the new Youth Home and Juvenile Assessment Center—designed to divert at-risk and court-involved youth—beginning with Priority 1 (16–24 beds plus 3 FTEs for the assessment center and 4.3 administrative FTEs) and scaling to 36 beds at Priority 3 with roughly $720,000 in conservative projected revenues. Discussion centered on acute recruitment challenges, with Nunn reporting a 52% vacancy rate updated during the session to 57%, prompting calls for a $50,000–$52,000 starting salary, pay compression relief, and overtime-rule adjustments before opening.

agenda_items.title: Day 1 Wrap-Up and Day 2 Schedule Confirmation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Manager Sowell and commissioners confirmed Day 2 topics, encouraged commissioners to email budget questions overnight to Budget Director Keith Lane, and agreed to reserve Board priority discussion time at the end of Day 2 (9:00 AM–12:00 PM with box lunches available if extended).

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Pledge, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the public charge, Commissioner Heidi Carter led the Pledge of Allegiance, and Clerk Monica Wallace announced the 2023–24 Durham Youth Leadership Fund grants ($500–$8,000). The Board then voted 5-0 to approve the minutes of the January 3, 2023 and February 6, 2023 meetings.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Black History Month Youth, Layne Riggs, Women's History Month, and Willie S. Darby
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board hosted Black History Month youth poetry readings, read a proclamation honoring Bahama/Durham County native Layne Riggs for winning the 2022 NASCAR Advance Auto Parts Weekly Series national championship at age 20, and proclaimed Women's History Month 2023. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns then read a resolution honoring retiring former Acting County Attorney Willie S. Darby for 14 years of service across two tenures, followed by remarks from Darby and his family.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendments (Articles 12 and 15 — Sedimentation and Erosion Control)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A resident spoke in support of proposed Unified Development Ordinance amendments protecting Southeast Durham's Triassic soils and strengthening enforcement, thanking Ryan Eaves and Sara Young while raising concerns about developments annexed into the city within the Falls Lake watershed. After closing the public hearing, the Board unanimously adopted the ordinance revising Article 12 (Infrastructure and Public Improvements) and Article 15 (Enforcement) and adopted the N.C.G.S. 160D-605 consistency statement.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0119: Amended Motion for Kempower Performance Agreement ($290,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns noted that in an earlier motion on Item 23-0119 she had said 'the county' instead of authorizing the County Manager, and conferred with the clerk to correct the record. Her amended motion authorizing the County Manager to negotiate and execute a $290,000 performance agreement with Kempower passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0117: Initial Resolution for Not-to-Exceed $235 Million Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A and 2023B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director Susan Tezai presented the initial resolution authorizing negotiation of an installment financing contract amendment for up to $235 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (converting the 2020/2021 draw program to long-term fixed-rate financing) and setting a March 13, 2023 public hearing. Commissioner Heidi Carter asked whether the action increased obligated debt, which Tezai confirmed reflected long-term issuance of debt obligated under the April 2021 draw program. The Board approved the resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Ballot Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Attorney announced ballot appointment results for six advisory bodies: Takeeba Call (Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee), Darryl Glover (Board of Health optometrist seat), Jeffrey Backelchuk, Deborah Green and Michael Vanpran (Historic Preservation Commission), Libria Stevenson (Juvenile Crime Prevention Council), and Carl Newman (Library Board of Trustees).

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (Confidential Records and Case No. 23-CVS-664)
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the statutory grounds under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) and (a)(3) regarding Case No. 23-CVS-664 (Fulton and General Woods v. Sarah Bradshaw). The motion was seconded and approved by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of January 3, 2023 and February 6, 2023 Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to approve the January 3, 2023 and February 6, 2023 work session/regular session minutes as noted; after a second, the motion passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Ordinance Amending UDO Article 12 (Infrastructure and Public Improvements) and Article 15 (Enforcement)
votes.discussion_detail: After closing the public hearing on UDO sedimentation and erosion control revisions, a commissioner moved to adopt the ordinance amending Articles 12 and 15 of the Unified Development Ordinance. The motion was seconded and passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Statement of Consistency Pursuant to N.C.G.S. 160D-605 (UDO Articles 12 and 15)
votes.notes: Confirmed as already voted on by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns at 03:23:25.
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to adopt the appropriate statement of consistency pursuant to N.C.G.S. 160D-605 for the UDO Articles 12 and 15 amendments; Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded, and the Board approved it by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0119: Amended Motion Authorizing County Manager to Execute $290,000 Kempower Performance Agreement
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved to amend the prior motion on Item 23-0119 so that the Board authorized the County Manager to negotiate and execute a $290,000 performance agreement with Kempower (replacing the earlier phrasing). Seconded and approved unanimously by voice vote, superseding the first motion.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0117: Initial Resolution for Not-to-Exceed $235M Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2023A/2023B) and Call for March 13 Public Hearing
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to adopt the initial resolution for the not-to-exceed $235 million Limited Obligation Bonds Series 2023A and 2023B, approve the identified financing team, and call a public hearing for March 13, 2023. Seconded and passed 5-0 by voice vote.

meetings.title: Board of County Commissioners Work Session for Feb. 6, 2023
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the February 6, 2023 work session, opening with acknowledgments of Black History Month, condolences over a recent young man's death, and a ceremonial recognition of Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisor David Harris as statewide Supervisor of the Year. Commissioners reviewed 19 consent agenda items—including DPS lottery capital reallocations, excise tax refund delegation, detention center padded-cell protocols, sewer maintenance contracts, IT renewals, and stormwater/erosion inspector staffing for 280 active sites. After suspending the rules for time-sensitive items, the Board approved a Sheriff's Office IIR grant extension through the end of February (rules suspended 3-0) and Item 23-0077, a letter of support for a General Services EPA grant application. On Item 23-0107, the Board suspended the rules, voted to rescind its January 23 vote on Item 23-0063 (a PERK local-match ILA with the City), and approved a $2 million contract through June 30, 2024 with the National Institute of Minority Economic Development to serve as fiscal agent for the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Opening Remarks, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read the public charge and confirmed no citizens were signed up to speak in person or online. She acknowledged Black History Month and lifted up condolences regarding the recent killing of a young man on his way home, and Clerk Monica Wallace announced that 2023 DCo Cares nonprofit recipient applications were open through February 10.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0059: Ceremonial Recognition of David Harris (Soil and Water Supervisor of the Year)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Soil and Water staff and Brian Evans, Executive Director of the North Carolina Association of Soil and Water Conservation Districts, recognized David Harris for receiving the statewide 2023 Supervisor of the Year award on January 19, 2023. Commissioners thanked Harris for his leadership on soil health, water quality, education, and farmland preservation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (19 Items: DPS Capital, Detention Padded Cells, Utilities, IT, and Erosion Inspection)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Dr. Kimberly Sowell walked through the 19-item consent agenda, including Item 23-0001 (CPA 23PA0012 reallocating Public School Building Capital Fund lottery funds for DPS), Item 23-0029 (excise tax refund delegation), Item 23-0041 ($160,077 Cornerstone Detention Products amendment up to $168,080), Items 23-0047 and 23-0050 (utility/sewer amendments), Item 23-0055 (NCDEQ access at 721 Foster Street), and IT renewals with NWN and SAP. Commissioners asked the Sheriff's Office about monitoring policies for detainees undergoing withdrawal or mental health crisis in padded cells (staff stated policies were being developed) and questioned erosion/sedimentation staff on staffing capacity, learning that three inspectors and one supervisor were covering roughly 280 active sites.

agenda_items.title: Sheriff's Office IIR Grant Extension Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff clarified that the Sheriff's Office had already been awarded a grant extension by IIR running only through the end of February, requiring the Board to suspend the rules at the work session to authorize the County Manager to sign before the late-February regular meeting. The Board voted 3-0 to suspend the rules and approved the extension by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0077: Letter of Support for General Services EPA Grant Application
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services requested a letter of support for an Environmental Protection Agency grant application covering roughly 25 assisted agreements nationwide (at least one per EPA region). The Board moved to suspend the rules and approved the letter of support by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0107: Rescission of Item 23-0063 and $2 Million Contract with National Institute of Minority Economic Development (Hayti Reborn)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff requested that the Board first suspend the rules and rescind its January 23, 2023 vote on Item 23-0063 (which authorized a PERK local-match ILA with the City of Durham) in order to change fiscal agents. After rescinding Item 23-0063, the Board discussed quarterly reporting and administrative fee parity with United Way and voted to approve a $2 million contract through June 30, 2024 with the National Institute of Minority Economic Development to serve as fiscal agent for the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement.

agenda_items.title: Item 23-0102: Commissioner Comments (Boards & Commissions Parity, Housing, and Tracker Updates)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed standardizing stipends, gifts, and budget support across joint city-county boards and commissions in advance of the upcoming budget season, reflected on collaborations with housing providers, and reviewed pending items on the Board's follow-up tracker including scheduling recognitions for former County Attorney Willie Darby and former Congressman David Price.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Sheriff's Office IIR Grant Extension
votes.notes: Chair announced 3-0; two commissioners were away from the dais at the time of the vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Because the IIR grant extension ran only through the end of February and could not wait until the late-February regular meeting, a commissioner moved to suspend the rules. Seconded and passed 3-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Sheriff's Office IIR Grant Extension Through February
votes.notes: Exact tally not announced aloud on the main motion.
votes.discussion_detail: Following suspension of the rules, the Board moved, seconded, and approved the Sheriff's Office IIR grant extension and authorized the County Manager to sign it.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0077: Suspend Rules and Approve Letter of Support for General Services EPA Grant Application
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to suspend the rules and support General Services' EPA grant application; after brief clarification on the regional award structure and a second, the motion passed by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Rescission of Item 23-0063
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to suspend the rules in order to vote on rescinding the January 23, 2023 approval of Item 23-0063. Seconded and passed by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Rescind January 23, 2023 Vote on Item 23-0063 (PERK ILA with City of Durham)
votes.discussion_detail: A commissioner moved to rescind the Board's January 23, 2023 vote on Agenda Item 23-0063 (entering an ILA with the City of Durham as local match for the PERK program benefiting the Hayti Reborn movement) so the county could instead contract directly with a new fiscal agent. Passed by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Item 23-0107: $2 Million Contract with National Institute of Minority Economic Development (Hayti Reborn Justice Movement Fiscal Agent)
votes.discussion_detail: Following discussion confirming quarterly reporting requirements, matching United Way administrative fees, and a contract end date of June 30, 2024, the Board voted by voice vote to approve the $2 million contract with the National Institute of Minority Economic Development as fiscal agent for the Hayti Reborn Justice Movement.
