meetings.title: Joint BOCC-BOE Meeting 8.17.21
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the August 17, 2021 joint meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners and the Durham Public Schools Board of Education (with BOE Chair Bettina Umstead), attended initially by four commissioners (Commissioner Nimasheena Burns joined later in the session). The joint boards unanimously approved May 18, 2021 joint minutes before reviewing Pre-K expansion (growing from 61 to 68 classrooms by 2022–23 and implementing a new Durham PreK Equity Plan) and DPS's FY22 budget ($169 million total county support, $250 teacher supplement increase, $31 million charter pass-through, and challenges hiring school nurses and replacing $2 million/year student hotspots). County Interim Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane then outlined the FY22–FY31 Capital Improvement Plan refresh and November 2022 General Obligation Bond referendum timeline, warning that 20%–80% construction cost inflation and 200%–375% steel/lumber spikes constrain debt affordability. Superintendent Pascal Mubenga closed by requesting Sheriff traffic support and expanded 7 AM–7 PM COVID-19 testing access for school reopening.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of May 18, 2021 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer called roll at 9:00 AM with Commissioners Howerton, Jacobs, Allam, and Carter and Board of Education Chair Bettina Umstead, Vice Chair Lewis, Member Raven, and Member Beyer present (Commissioner Burns joined later). Following Vice Chair Jacobs's note on two name corrections included in the morning packet update, the joint boards approved the May 18, 2021 minutes unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Early Learning, DPS Pre-K Expansion, and Durham PreK Equity Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Deputy Superintendent Nakia Hardy and Assistant Superintendent Dr. Debbie Pittman presented early learning alignment with the strategic plan, the Countdown to Kindergarten portal, ESL enrollment support, and Universal Pre-K Facilitator Stephanie Humphrey, detailing growth from 61 classrooms (784 seats) to 65 (858 seats) in 2021–22 and 68 (914 seats) in 2022–23 with Lyons Farm Elementary, plus pre-K capacity in Elementary F and renovated schools (per Matthew Palmer). CCSA's Linda Chappelle reported 1,607 pre-K applications (up from 1,296), $917–$1,834 COVID hazard bonuses for pre-K staff, and a new Durham PreK Equity Plan prioritizing wrap-around care, Spanish-speaking teachers, and transportation, hoping to leverage ARPA funds toward the 3,600-seat goal.

agenda_items.title: DPS Budget, State Legislative Outlook, Charter Pass-Through, and School Nurses/Hotspots Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS CFO Paul LeSieur thanked the county for over $11 million in new FY22 appropriations ($169M total county support), funding a $250 certified/teacher supplement raise (over $5,600/year), $6M capital outlay, $500,000 for English learners, two counselors, and 10 additional school nurses, while noting $31M flows to charter schools and roughly $15M+ could come to DPS if $730M in statewide fines/forfeitures are released. LeSieur and Chappelle clarified how state NC Pre-K payments are capped at $320/month for DPS vs. $1,250/month local Durham PreK funding, and officials discussed $2M annual student hotspot costs and severe difficulty recruiting 10+ vacant school nurses amid $10,000–$20,000 hospital sign-on bonuses.

agenda_items.title: County Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Refresh and 2022 General Obligation Bond Referendum Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Manager Claudia Hager updated the boards on rural broadband planning as a top county priority, and Budget Director Keith Lane outlined the FY22–FY31 CIP update and November 8, 2022 GO bond referendum schedule (culminating from fall 2021 facility assessments, February market testing, and summer 2022 LGC approvals). Hager and Lane cautioned that labor shortages, 200% steel and 375% lumber price spikes, and 20%–80% project cost inflation strain county debt capacity ($60M–$70M annual debt service split ~50/50 between DPS and county projects) without property tax rate increases, while commissioners and BOE members discussed green building investments, MWBE participation with the Institute, and quarterly CIP updates.

agenda_items.title: School Reopening Closing Remarks: Mask Mandate, Traffic, and COVID-19 Testing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOE Chair Bettina Umstead thanked commissioners for adopting the countywide indoor mask mandate and backed the 2022 bond, while Superintendent Pascal Mubenga requested Sheriff and city traffic support during the first two weeks of school and 7 AM–7 PM community COVID testing access. The meeting adjourned at 11:00 AM, with the next joint session hosted by the Board of Education on November 16, 2021.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 18, 2021 Joint Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint meeting vote tally was 4-0 among BOCC members present (8-0 combined including BOE Chair Bettina Umstead, Vice Chair Lewis, Member Raven, and Member Beyer). Commissioner Nimasheena Burns joined later in the session. Mover and seconder not explicitly named.
votes.discussion_detail: After confirming two name revisions requested by Vice Chair Jacobs were included in the morning packet update, participating BOCC and BOE members voted unanimously to approve the May 18, 2021 joint minutes.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Meeting Aug 9, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the August 9, 2021 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners, with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved five sets of prior minutes and 21 consent items, while pulling Item 21-0491 to read and adopt the Durham County Language Equity Policy Resolution by a separate 5-0 vote. Ceremonial items recognized Register of Deeds Sharon Davis's international leadership, the Sheriff's Office National Sheriffs' Association Triple Crown accreditation (21-0451), and the Durham Digital Equity Plan (21-0484). Commissioners also held a public hearing on a $125,000 economic development incentive for Smart Wires Inc. (leaving comments open 24 hours), received a COVID-19 briefing on the county's newly enacted 5:00 PM indoor mask mandate and fourth-wave Delta surge, agreed to issue a support letter for adding Camp Butner to the NC Sentinel Landscape Partnership, and met in closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Commissioner Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Vice Chair Jacobs asked to ensure Item 21-0491 (Language Equity Policy Resolution) would be read aloud, and Chair Howerton agreed to pull it from consent. Clerk Monica Toomer read announcements on the August 20 Back to School Bash, vaccine clinic hours, 2021 property tax billing with partial payments, Durham Pre-K, P-EBT expansion, Register of Deeds vital-record appointments, 911 hiring, convenience site hours, and the newly reopened Main Library, while Vice Chair Jacobs highlighted $3.31 million in ERAP rent relief disbursed since June 1 and two DSS social workers stationed at the courthouse.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (May 18, May 27, June 3, June 7, and June 28, 2021)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered five sets of minutes (May 18, May 27, June 3 budget meeting, June 7 work session, and June 28 regular session) with no edits offered. All five sets were approved together by a 5-0 roll-call vote.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Register of Deeds Recognition, Sheriff's Triple Crown Award (21-0451), and Digital Equity Plan Resolution (21-0484)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton recognized Register of Deeds Sharon Davis for her international leadership role. Chief Deputy Whited, Lt. Hartigan, and Sgt. Kusher accepted recognition for the Sheriff's Office becoming 1 of 49 agencies nationally (and 2nd in NC) to earn the Triple Crown accreditation (CALEA, NCCHC, and ACA), and Chair Howerton read Resolution 21-0484 adopting the Durham Digital Equity Plan, joined by Library Director Tammy Baggett, Digital Durham founder Laura Fogle, and Claudia Tooms (noting the Stanford L. Warren digital navigator grant, Item 21-0453).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (21 Items, Excluding Item 21-0491)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 21-0491 (Language Equity Resolution) was pulled for reading, and Vice Chair Jacobs requested that quarterly performance reports under grant Item 21-0474 be shared with the board via the County Manager. Commissioner Burns moved and Commissioner Carter seconded approval of the 21 remaining consent items, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 21-0491: Durham County Language Equity Policy Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jacobs read the resolution enacting the Durham County Language Access Policy to remove communication barriers through expanded translations (beginning with Spanish) and closed captioning. General Manager Deborah Craig-Ray thanked the board for supporting the initiative, and commissioners unanimously approved the resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0499: Economic Development Incentive Allocation for Smart Wires Inc. ($125,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andy Miracle presented a $125,000 performance-based grant for Smart Wires Inc. to relocate its corporate headquarters from San Francisco to Durham, creating 250 jobs and $23.5 million in investment alongside a state JDIG award and partnerships with DPS CTE, Durham Tech, and the Research Triangle Cleantech Cluster. Chief People Officer Shannon Ross affirmed local hiring and clean-grid commitments, Commissioner Burns criticized state press releases for omitting county officials and staff, and the public hearing was left open 24 hours through August 10 ahead of an August 23 vote.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Held open 24 hours / Vote deferred to Aug. 23

agenda_items.title: Other Business Item 21-0492: Public Health COVID-19 Update and Indoor Mask Mandate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Health Directors Liz Stevens and Kristen Patterson detailed the county's new State of Emergency indoor mask mandate effective at 5:00 PM for ages 5+, reporting a Delta-driven fourth wave (70 cases/day 7-day average, 4.6% positivity, 54.1% total / 62.9% 12+ fully vaccinated per CDC, 20% July breakthrough cases, and 23% July cases under age 18) and the new $100 first-dose/$25 driver cash card incentive. Commissioners requested 12–18 vaccination rates, urged expanding incentives to minors ages 12–17, called for clearer online testing site listings, and heard Stevens explain that BinaxNOW rapid antigen tests have roughly 40% sensitivity compared to PCR tests.

agenda_items.title: Other Business Item 21-0493: North Carolina Sentinel Landscape Partnership Support Letter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Deborah Craig-Ray introduced Dr. Mary Lou Addor of NC State University, who presented the 33-county Eastern NC Sentinel Landscape Partnership coordinating military readiness, farmland and forest conservation easements, flood catchments, and carbon sequestration. She requested a county support letter by August 26 to add Camp Butner (Durham and Granville counties) and MOTSU to the federal designation; Commissioners Burns and Jacobs endorsed the effort and Chair Howerton instructed staff to prepare the letter for signature.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (consensus to issue support letter)

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development Incentives — G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss industrial/business location or expansion and tentative economic development incentives. Returning to open session at 02:51:20, Chair Howerton announced direction was given to staff and the board voted 5-0 to adjourn.

meetings.title: BOCC - August 2, 2021 Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the August 2, 2021 virtual work session with all five commissioners, Interim County Manager Claudia Hager, and Acting County Attorney Willie Darby present. During citizen comments and consent agenda review, the board heard an emailed comment opposing COVID-19 restrictions and reviewed multiple of the 20 consent items, including HVAC procurement evaluation and MWBE participation, a Library Digital Navigators grant, a $3.3 million NCDHHS public health grant, a $75,000 immunization grant, and Board of Elections and EMS billing contract amendments. After suspending the rules (5-0), the board voted 5-0 to appoint Chair Howerton as voting delegate and Commissioner Nida Allam as alternate to the NCACC 114th Annual Conference. Commissioners also discussed NACo conference takeaways on ARPA processes, food security cold-storage grants, the Delta variant, and the expiration of the federal eviction moratorium before entering and returning from a closed session under attorney-client privilege.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the work session to order, read the public charge, and noted a 3:30 p.m. call scheduled with the Mayor and Public Health Director. Clerk Monica Wallace read one emailed citizen comment from Kimberly Israel opposing the reinstatement of COVID-19 masking and distancing restrictions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Items 21-0449, 22-BC-007, 21-0454, and Related Contracts)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager walked through items from the 20-item consent agenda ahead of the upcoming regular session. Warren with Digital Durham, reviewed a $3.3 million NCDHHS epidemiology/communicable disease grant (21-0454) and a $75,000 immunization grant, and clarified Board of Elections, DPS shelter MOA, Evergreen Services, and EMS billing fee amendments (21-0462).

agenda_items.title: Appointment of NCACC 114th Annual Conference Voting Delegate and Alternate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle digest omission, the board took up appointing a voting delegate and alternate for the August 12–14 NCACC annual conference. Because Commissioner Heidi Carter switched to virtual attendance, Commissioner Nida Allam replaced Carter as alternate; Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs briefly asked about rotating the voting delegate role to newer commissioners, and the board agreed to continue rotating at future conferences. The board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to appoint Chair Howerton as voting delegate and Commissioner Allam as alternate.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments and Review of Directives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nida Allam yielded her comment time to Commissioner Nimasheena Burns, who reported on the NACo conference and praised Durham's ARPA planning relative to counties using full participatory budgeting. Commissioners also discussed a USDA cold-storage feasibility grant for food security, the Delta variant, and urging landlords to participate in rental assistance following expiration of the federal eviction moratorium, followed by a brief directives tracker check-in from Drew Cummings.

meetings.title: BOCC - Budget Work Session: Day 4
meetings.executive_summary: During Day 4 of the FY2021-22 budget work sessions (addressed by Chair Brenda A. Howerton on June 3, 2021 and published June 4, 2021), commissioners reviewed Durham County's behavioral health infrastructure and the budget add/delete list with no formal votes taken. Criminal Justice Resource Center Director Gudrun Parmer and Behavioral Health stakeholders reviewed the Stepping Up Initiative, sequential intercept mapping, mental health court, and diversion gaps. A policy disagreement emerged when an unidentified commissioner suggested freezing unfilled Sheriff's Office positions to fund unarmed behavioral health crisis responders, which the Durham County Sheriff strongly opposed amid high gun-violence rates and staffing vacancies, advocating instead for federal ARPA/CARES funding and a law-enforcement-centered co-responder model. Later in the session, commissioners and staff discussed base budget revenue growth, the Master Aging Plan placeholder, deliverables for the Black Chamber of Commerce request, shifting resources from the underutilized tax deferral program to the tax grant program, and late fund-balance adjustments for RTP tax valuations and Risk Management insurance premiums before canceling the June 9 session.

agenda_items.title: Item 20-3078: Behavioral Health Infrastructure and Crisis Response Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Gudrun Parmer and behavioral health partners reviewed the 2015 Stepping Up Initiative resolution, sequential intercept mapping, de-escalation training, mental health court, and LME/MCO coordination with Alliance. Debate arose over crisis response staffing: an unidentified commissioner proposed testing an unarmed behavioral health/paramedicine response by freezing unfilled law enforcement positions, while the Sheriff opposed any position freezes or 10% budget cut given nearly 1,000 shootings and existing vacancies, urging ARPA/CARES funding and law enforcement participation in co-responder design.

agenda_items.title: Budget Add/Delete List, Tax Relief Programs, and Late Fund Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle digest omission, Interim Manager Claudia Hager and budget staff reviewed the add/delete list and base budget philosophy that tax increases should be an absolute last choice. Commissioner Heidi Carter and another commissioner questioned deliverables on the Black Chamber of Commerce proposal; Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked whether staffing from the tax deferral program (which had only one applicant) could shift toward the tax grant program; and David Ades presented fund-balance-covered adjustments for the RTP special district valuation and a Risk Management insurance premium increase, before the board agreed to drop the June 9 work session and adjourn ahead of June 14 budget adoption.

disagreements.issue: Freezing Unfilled Law Enforcement Positions to Fund Unarmed Behavioral Health Crisis Responders
disagreements.summary: During the behavioral health infrastructure presentation, an unidentified commissioner and the Durham County Sheriff disagreed over whether unfilled Sheriff's Office positions should be frozen to fund behavioral health crisis response specialists versus using federal ARPA/CARES funds while keeping law enforcement centered in co-responder models.
disagreements.side_a_position: Freeze unfilled law enforcement positions and reallocate duties to behavioral health specialists for non-armed crisis response.
side_a_arguments: Communities are asking to decriminalize behavioral health challenges, poverty, and homelessness and reduce racial bias in crisis response.
Reorganizing unfilled positions rather than cutting filled roles avoids punitive action against officers while scaling non-armed response such as paramedicine.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not freeze Sheriff's Office positions or cut 10% of the Sheriff's budget; fund behavioral health response with ARPA/CARES dollars and include law enforcement at the center of co-responder models.
side_b_arguments: The Sheriff's Office is already short-staffed amid nearly 1,000 shootings and over 129 shooting victims in Durham's Black and brown communities.
Ample federal CARES and American Rescue Plan funds are available for behavioral health initiatives, and established models like CAHOOTS operate in coordination with law enforcement.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken during the work session; both sides agreed on continuing collaboration around crisis response models.

meetings.title: BOCC - Budget Work Session: Day 3
meetings.executive_summary: At Day 3 of the FY2021-22 budget work sessions on June 1, 2021, Chair Brenda A. Howerton and commissioners reviewed workforce development, employee compensation, and community violence intervention proposals with no formal votes taken. Durham Technical Community College President JB Buxton presented the $500,000 manager-recommended request and potential ARPA expansion for the 'Back to Work' short-term training program and the 'BULLS' life sciences pipeline for young adults of color, including wraparound stipends for childcare and transportation. Commissioners and HR/budget staff then examined county salary competitiveness, lagging 2017 pay bands, longevity pay, and the balance between rising personnel costs (~85% of the county budget) and lifting wages for the 47% of county workers earning $49,000 or less. Finally, General Manager Joanne Pierce outlined plans to consolidate Bull City United, My Brother's Keeper, and Project BUILD into a new department expanding from 16 to 36 staff in partnership with Cure Violence Global before the board adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0364: Durham Technical Community College Budget Request (Back to Work & BULLS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Tech President JB Buxton presented the college's workforce recovery budget request centered on two initiatives: 'Back to Work' (short-term 6–8 week courses under $1,000 with $500 scholarships and wraparound stipends for childcare, transportation, and books) and 'BULLS' (biowork and life sciences training, coaching, and job placement for 18–24-year-old students of color and opportunity youth). Buxton detailed how the $500,000 in the manager's recommended budget plus potential one-time federal ARPA dollars could fund facility renovations, campus planning, direct student stipends, and specialized corporate and financial aid staffing.

agenda_items.title: County Employee Compensation, Market Bands, and Workforce Retention
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle digest omission, HR and budget staff reviewed how county pay bands based on 2017 data continued to lag peer jurisdictions even after a 3% band adjustment, alongside prior hazard/risk adjustments for public safety, DSS, and EMS and the potential return of longevity pay. Commissioners noted that personnel accounts for roughly 85% of the county budget—requiring careful sustainability planning for new positions—while emphasizing that 47% of employees earn $49,000 or less annually and must be prioritized to reduce turnover.

agenda_items.title: New Departmental Structure for Bull City United, My Brother's Keeper, and Project BUILD
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Joanne Pierce presented the organizational plan to unify Bull City United, My Brother's Keeper, and Project BUILD into a single new department following City Council (March) and BOCC (April) interlocal funding approvals. Working with Cure Violence Global, the expansion increases total staffing from 16 to 36 positions, adding a department administrator and a data analyst to manage grant compliance and public reporting, with the next quarterly report due July 31.

agenda_items.title: Schedule Preview, Research Triangle Foundation Tour, and Closing Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager previewed upcoming work sessions on June 3 and June 9 (including a possible ARPA broadband update) and staff noted a future tour opportunity at Research Triangle Foundation's Boxyard project. Commissioner Nida Allam wished LGBTQIA residents and staff a Happy Pride, Chair Howerton acknowledged Memorial Day, and the meeting adjourned without a vote.

meetings.title: BOCC - May 27, 2021 - Budget Work Session Day 2
meetings.executive_summary: During Day 2 of the FY2021-22 budget work sessions on May 27, 2021, Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and early childhood staff briefed the board on American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding rules and early childhood pandemic impacts, with no formal votes taken. Hager outlined Durham County's $62.4 million ARPA allocation, federal obligation (December 31, 2024) and expenditure (2026) deadlines, GFOA guidance prioritizing FEMA reimbursements and one-time or transitional investments, and ~$2.9 million in initial FY22 ARPA allocations alongside candidate priorities such as $750,000 in homeowner tax relief, housing, behavioral health, Durham Tech workforce programs, food security, and Pre-K/K-12. Early childhood presenter Kate then detailed pandemic childcare closures, a 200% spike in diaper need, and early brain-development impacts, prompting Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and Budget Director Keith Lane to verify funding for Reach Out and Read ($50,000), Wash and Learn, and Article 46 Pre-K revenue before previewing the June 3 behavioral health work session.

agenda_items.title: American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Allocation Framework and FY22 Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager briefed the board on Durham County's $62.4 million ARPA allocation (half expected in June 2021 and half in 2022), eligible spending categories, U.S. Treasury reporting timelines, and GFOA best practices such as maximizing FEMA reimbursements, focusing on one-time or phased investments, centering equity and MWBE support, and coordinating community engagement with the City and Durham Public Schools. She reviewed ~$2.9 million already identified in the FY22 budget for COVID cleaning, screening security, and revenue losses ($48,000 and $265,000 court facility fees) plus candidate uses including $750,000 for DSS long-term homeowner relief (<=30% AMI), non-congregate housing, vaccine equity, behavioral health, workforce development, business support, food insecurity, and Pre-K/K-12.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Impacts on Early Childhood Systems and ARPA Opportunities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a middle digest omission, early childhood lead Kate presented pandemic impacts on Durham's early childhood sector, including permanent childcare closures, lower enrollment, staff burnout, a greater than 200% surge in diaper need, and housing/food instability affecting ages 0–5. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked for budget clarity on Reach Out and Read and Wash and Learn, highlighted Cooperative Extension's Welcome Baby and diaper demand, and noted Article 46 sales tax generated ~$75,000 for Pre-K, while Commissioners Nimasheena Burns and Chair Howerton emphasized aligning federal/state grants for early childhood.

agenda_items.title: June 3 Behavioral Health Session Preview and Budget Schedule Confirmation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff member Jody previewed the June 3 behavioral health work session involving Gudrun Parmer (Stepping Up Initiative), DSS, Public Health, CJRC, the Sheriff's Office, and Alliance. Budget Director Keith Lane confirmed $50,000 was budgeted for Reach Out and Read and committed to confirming Wash and Learn via email, and Interim Manager Hager announced the June 1 and June 3 budget session times before the board adjourned.

meetings.title: BOCC - May 24, 2021 Regular Session

Howerton and all five commissioners approved the April 26 and May 3 meeting minutes (5-0), welcomed newly hired Food Security Coordinator Mary Oxendine, and unanimously passed the five-item consent agenda (5-0), which included a $100,000 biotech award to GRAIL, a $3.21 million Snow Hill Pump Station capital amendment, NC Farm School funding, April tax releases, and an architectural contract for the former DSS Main Street building. meetings.title: BOCC Budget Work Session - Day 1
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over Day 1 of the Board of County Commissioners' FY2021-22 budget work session, held with all five seated commissioners and newly appointed Interim County Manager Claudia Hager following an earlier joint morning session with the Durham Public Schools (DPS) Board of Education. Budget Director Keith Lane and Hager reviewed the $18 million DPS request—of which the recommended budget funded roughly $8.2 million in new current expense and capital dollars—and led extensive discussion on DPS's late request for 20 additional school nurses and social workers, with commissioners favoring housing school nurses in the County Public Health Department on a phased hiring timeline to avoid the roughly 28% charter school per-pupil surcharge. Commissioners also debated community safety and mental health funding ahead of upcoming work sessions, with Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs proposing a crisis-response gaps analysis while Chair Howerton and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns urged consulting the new Community Safety and Wellness Task Force co-chairs and recognizing existing county mental health spending before shifting Sheriff's Office funds. Additional commissioner priorities flagged for subsequent May and June work sessions included Durham Pre-K, the Early Childhood Action Plan, Master Aging Plan staffing, northern Durham broadband via ARPA funds, coordinator role consolidation, and a shared county-city TV studio upgrade. No formal votes were taken during this informational work session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Budget Work Session Schedule Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the Day 1 budget work session to order (noting it followed the morning joint session with the Durham Public Schools Board of Education). Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane outlined the tentative work session calendar: May 24 budget public hearing, May 27 ARPA next-steps framework, vaccine equity proposal, DSS Medicaid support, and low-income homeowner tax subsidy (<=30% AMI), June 1 economic development, Durham Tech, Office of Sheriff peer comparisons, and maternal health infrastructure, plus a June 3 placeholder.

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools (DPS) Budget Request, School Nurses, and Federal ARPA Strategy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane explained that of DPS's $18 million funding request, the recommended budget included $7 million in general current expense plus $1.9 million for $15/hour wages and $1.13 million in additional current capital (bringing current capital to $4.5 million toward a $6 million request). Staff and commissioners discussed DPS's late request for 20 additional school nurses and social workers (roughly 18 nurses and 2–3 social workers), agreeing in principle to explore hiring nurses through the County Public Health Department on a phased schedule to avoid the 28% charter school pass-through surcharge and navigate regional nursing shortages. Interim Manager Hager also noted using one-time ARPA funds (~$1.2M for custodial cleaning) to avoid ongoing tax shocks, while Commissioners Carter, Jacobs, and Allam requested follow-up on English language learners, students with disabilities, IT refresh needs, and per-square-foot capital expenditure comparisons.

agenda_items.title: Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, Crisis Response Gaps Analysis, and Sheriff's Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter asked staff to consider packaging existing upstream safety and wellness programs across departments so the board and community—including advocates from Durham Beyond Policing and Durham For All—could assess current resources before shifting positions away from the Office of the Sheriff. Commissioner Nimasheena Burns cited CJRC Director Gudrun Parmer's preliminary mapping, legal mandates governing law enforcement calls, and roughly $30–40 million in existing county mental health spending (including jail clinical staff), urging concrete staffing plans rather than cutting the Sheriff's budget in a vacuum. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs suggested funding a comprehensive gaps analysis of the crisis response system in the upcoming budget, and Chair Howerton asked Interim Manager Hager to consult the task force co-chairs.

agenda_items.title: Additional Commissioner Budget Priorities, Coordinator Review, and TV Studio Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Carter and Jacobs highlighted early childhood priorities (Durham Pre-K, Reach Out and Read, Early Childhood Action Plan), the sustainability plan, Master Aging Plan staffing, language equity, and broadband expansion. Chair Howerton emphasized northern Durham broadband, climate, maternal health, and reviewing whether separate coordinator positions across county programs could be consolidated after budget season. General Manager Deborah Craig-Ray and Perry Mann also updated the board on using leftover Admin II capital funds to upgrade the county TV studio in a no-money broadcast-swap partnership with the City of Durham.

meetings.title: BOCC - Special Session - May 17, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton convened the May 17, 2021 special session with all five commissioners and Acting County Attorney Willie Darby present. After Commissioner Nimasheena Burns read the public charge, the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel under attorney-client privilege. Upon returning to open session after approximately 79 minutes, the board voted 5-0 on a motion by Commissioner Nida Allam, seconded by Commissioner Heidi Carter, to appoint Claudia Hager as Interim County Manager. Chair Howerton noted she voted yes reluctantly due to the circumstances that created the vacancy while thanking Hager for reassuring county employees, and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs thanked both Hager and county staff before the board adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Appointment of Claudia Hager as Interim County Manager

meetings.title: BOCC - Special Session - May 13, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the contentious May 13, 2021 special session with all five commissioners, Acting County Attorney Willie Darby, and outside counsel Denise Smith Klein present. After voting 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3), the board returned to open session and passed three deeply divided 3-2 votes initiated by Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs: (1) not renewing County Manager Wendell Davis's contract, terminating it effective June 29, 2021 (Ayes: Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nays: Nimasheena Burns, Brenda A. Howerton); (2) relieving Davis of his duties effective immediately pending appointment of an interim manager (Ayes: Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nays: Nimasheena Burns, Brenda A. Howerton); and (3) extending outside attorney Denise Smith Klein's contract to execute the board's decisions (Ayes: Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nays: Nimasheena Burns, Brenda A. Howerton). During debate, Chair Howerton and Commissioner Burns sharply condemned the non-renewal as retaliatory, racially motivated, and lacking merit or a formal performance appraisal, while also objecting that the outside counsel extension lacked a confirmed total cost. A final motion to adjourn was also contested on roll call, passing with Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, and Wendy Jacobs voting Aye, Nimasheena Burns voting No, and Chair Howerton declaring the motion carried and adjourning the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton called the May 13, 2021 special session to order, read the public charge, and cited N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel (Acting County Attorney Willie Darby and outside attorney Denise Smith Klein). On a motion by Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded by Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, the board entered closed session 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Non-Renewal of County Manager Wendell Davis's Employment Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon returning to open session, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved under Section 4 of the County Manager's contract not to renew the agreement, terminating it on June 29, 2021 while complying with all contractual obligations. Chair Brenda A. Howerton stated the decision was made without discussion with Black board members and praised Davis's seven-year record on finances and schools, while Commissioner Nimasheena Burns read a prepared statement condemning the motion as racially motivated retaliation following Davis's 2020 racial bias complaint and citing the Coleman Report and lack of a performance appraisal. The motion passed 3-2 on roll call.

agenda_items.title: Immediate Relief of County Manager Duties
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved to relieve County Manager Wendell Davis of his duties effective immediately and proceed to appoint an interim county manager. Following a second, the board approved the motion 3-2 on a roll-call vote with Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, and Wendy Jacobs in favor and Nimasheena Burns and Brenda A. Howerton opposed.

agenda_items.title: Extension of Outside Counsel Denise Smith Klein's Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs moved to extend outside attorney Denise Smith Klein's existing contract to assist with executing the board's decisions and obligations, clarified as an extension at her existing hourly rate after Acting Attorney Willie Darby advised an RFP was not required to extend an existing contract. Chair Howerton and Commissioner Burns objected that no price cap or confirmed rate for expanded services had been provided and warned of wasted funds and litigation risk, while Commissioner Carter affirmed her readiness and seconded the motion. The motion passed 3-2.

agenda_items.title: Contested Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Acting Attorney Darby noted Klein could decline the extension terms if she wished (requiring renegotiation), a motion to adjourn was made and seconded. On roll call, Commissioners Allam, Carter, and Jacobs voted Aye, Commissioner Burns voted No, and Chair Howerton declared the vote carried and adjourned the meeting.

disagreements.issue: Non-Renewal and Immediate Relief of County Manager Wendell Davis
disagreements.summary: The board split 3-2 over Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs's motions to not renew County Manager Wendell Davis's contract (terminating June 29, 2021) and to relieve him of his duties immediately.
disagreements.side_a_position: Exercise Section 4 of the County Manager's contract to not renew his agreement and relieve him of duties immediately pending an interim appointment.
side_a_arguments: Board has contractual authority under Section 4 to decide on non-renewal and comply with all contract obligations.
Board needed an immediate transition to an interim county manager.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose non-renewal and immediate removal as unwarranted, racially motivated, and procedurally unfair.
side_b_arguments: Decision was made without consulting Black board members and without completing a formal performance appraisal or board training.
Wendell Davis maintained seven straight years of strong county financial standing and school-building progress.
Action constituted retaliation for Davis and county staff raising racial bias concerns, while failing to implement Coleman Report and Racial Equity Task Force recommendations.
disagreements.resolution: Both motions passed 3-2 on roll-call votes (Ayes: Allam, Carter, Jacobs; Nays: Burns, Howerton).

disagreements.issue: Extension of Outside Attorney Denise Smith Klein's Contract Without Confirmed Total Cost
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split 3-2 over extending outside counsel Denise Smith Klein's contract to assist with executing the manager contract termination and related obligations.
disagreements.side_a_position: Extend Klein's existing contract at her existing hourly rate to assist with executing all obligations flowing from the board's decisions.
side_a_arguments: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby advised that extending an existing contract did not require a new RFP.
An existing hourly rate was already set in Klein's current engagement, making the motion sufficiently definite.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose extending the contract without a confirmed cost ceiling, RFP, or Klein's confirmation of rates for expanded scope.
side_b_arguments: Klein's prior contract covered only document review, whereas execution work could entail different costs.
Voting on a contract without a defined price or prior board discussion of cost violates sound fiscal stewardship and risks litigation.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 3-2 (Ayes: Allam, Carter, Jacobs; Nays: Burns, Howerton), with Acting Attorney Darby noting Klein could decline the extension terms.

meetings.title: BOCC May10 2021  Durham County
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the May 10, 2021 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (captured in this recording starting mid-announcements), with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved prior minutes (5-0), issued four ceremonial proclamations (Children's Mental Health Awareness Month, Cooperative Extension Week, Older Americans Month, and National Foster Care Month), recognized the Board of Elections for winning a U.S. Election Assistance Commission 2020 Clearinghouse Award, and approved all 14 consent agenda items 5-0, including $12.438 million for IS&T capital modernization and $92.785 million in limited obligation bonds for Northern High School. Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported declining COVID-19 case trends alongside FDA emergency use authorization for Pfizer vaccinations for ages 12 and older, and County Manager Wendell Davis presented the proposed ~$730 million FY2021-22 recommended budget featuring a 1-cent general fund property tax increase, 3% employee COLA plus merit pay reinstatement, $163.3 million for Durham Public Schools, and $750,000 for a long-time homeowner tax relief grant program. The board also received annual reports from the Appearance Commission and Open Space and Trails Commission and held public hearings on Palmer Way renaming and UDO Omnibus Text Amendment TC2100001, leaving both open for 24-hour comment ahead of May 24 votes.

agenda_items.title: Announcements and Commissioner Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: This recording begins mid-announcements as Clerk Monica Toomer read notices on Food for Durham, Real ID enforcement updates, DCHC MPO long-range transportation plan comments, and a workaround link after a technical glitch delayed the Durham Emergency Rental Assistance Program (ERAP) launch. Commissioners thanked nurses for National Nurses Week, praised DSS Director Ben Rose and staff member Janine Gordon for ERAP rollout efforts, and Commissioner Nida Allam shared mutual-aid resources for COVID-19 relief in India.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (April 5 Work Session and April 12 Regular Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the minutes of the April 5, 2021 work session and April 12, 2021 regular session without edits. Commissioner Heidi Carter moved approval, seconded by Commissioner Nida Allam, and the minutes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations (Mental Health, Cooperative Extension, Older Americans, Foster Care) and Board of Elections Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners read four proclamations: Children's Mental Health Awareness Month (21-0237, accepted by Tika Dobson and Alliance Health CEO Rob Robinson, who discussed a forthcoming 16-bed regional child crisis facility), Cooperative Extension Week (accepted by Donna Rewalt and Chrystal Gibson), Older Americans Month (accepted by DSS Director Ben Rose and Janine Gordon), and National Foster Care Month (21-0283, accepted by Ben Rose and Jovetta Whitfield, noting 306 children in Durham foster care). At [00:58:19], the board also recognized Board of Elections Chair Phil Lehman and Director Derek Bowens (Item 21-0304) for winning a 2020 U.S. Election Assistance Commission Clearinghouse Award for their early voting wait-time tracking tool.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (14 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis reviewed all 14 consent items, including Item 205 ($12,438,000 IS&T capital project amendment), Item 248 (City-County sodium chloride storage ILA), Item 255 ($130,412 sewer utility capital transfer), Item 260 ($60,000 Convention Center roof fireproofing), Item 261 ($1,034 CJRC donation), Items 263 and 273 (David Young Utilities contracts), Item 267 (FY22 Transit Work Program and material change), Item 274 (NCDOT Riddle Road widening support resolution), Item 282 ($325,428.60 Sheriff Office 365 migration), Item 284 (janitorial services RFP), Item 292 ($92,785,075 LOBs capital amendment for Northern High School), Item 293 (JCPC multi-year funding), and Item 306 (NIED DPS MWBE contract amendment). Vice Chair Jacobs highlighted full funding for Northern High School and Commissioner Burns commended JCPC multi-year funding before the board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0270: Public Health COVID-19 Focus Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 25 active COVID-19 cases, 227 cumulative deaths, and 25,409 total cases, with 41.6% of Durham's total population and 80.1% of seniors vaccinated and community transmission dropping from high to substantial. He highlighted persistent overrepresentation of Black residents in new cases (60.78%), expanding Latinx vaccine turnout (28% partial, 20% full), walk-in hours, community paramedic outreach to unhoused residents, and preparations to vaccinate ages 12 and up following FDA emergency use authorization for Pfizer.

agenda_items.title: FY2021-22 County Manager's Recommended Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis presented the proposed FY2021-22 budget totaling nearly $730 million across all funds (and nearly $500 million General Fund, up 6.89%), recommending a 1-cent general fund property tax rate increase ($4.58M) plus a 1-cent Durham County Fire & Rescue Service District increase and 0.75-cent Lebanon Fire District increase. Key investments included $163.3 million for Durham Public Schools (+$10.1M total), $500,000 for Durham Tech workforce/BULLS pipelines, a 3% employee COLA plus 2%–3% merit pay reinstatement, $750,000 plus 3 FTEs for a Long-Time Homeowner Tax Relief Grant Program (<=30% AMI), Bull City United expansion into a standalone department, 10 DSS Medicaid quality assurance FTEs, 39 Sheriff vehicles, Justice Center court parking validation, a $1M public safety storage lease, 4.76% sewer rate increase, 2 racial equity FTEs, and ~$2.9M in ARPA offsets. Chair Howerton noted discussion would begin in work sessions rather than that evening.

agenda_items.title: Items 21-0285 & 21-0286: City-County Appearance Commission and Open Space & Trails (DOST) 2020 Annual Reports
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Kayla Seibel presented the Appearance Commission 2020 Annual Report, prompting Commissioner Burns to ask about addressing members with 20–30% attendance rates despite excused absences. Senior Planner Carl Kolosna presented the DOST 2020 Annual Report noting four matching grants totaling over $77,000 against $190,000 in requests, and Vice Chair Jacobs urged restoring the DOST matching grant budget from $77,175 back to its pre-2008 level of $100,000.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0288: Palmer Way Street Renaming to Alexandria Way
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Cole Renigar and Planning Director Sara Young presented an applicant-initiated request to rename Palmer Way (between T.W. Alexander Drive and Ellis Road) to Alexandria Way, noting adjacent parcels are owned by the applicant and reviewing agencies had no objections. No callers or speakers signed up; Chair Howerton opened the 24-hour comment window closing May 11 and deferred the vote to May 24.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Public hearing held / Vote deferred to May 24

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing Item 21-0289: UDO Text Amendment Omnibus Changes 16 (TC2100001)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock and Planning Director Sara Young presented UDO Text Amendment TC2100001 (recommended 11-1 by the Planning Commission and approved May 3 by City Council), covering technical revisions, co-living parking parity (removing the term 'co-housing'), Commercial General height consistency (50 to 55 feet), and maximum driveway width expansion from 25 to 30 feet. Staff clarified to Commissioner Carter that Northgate Mall is zoned CC and unaffected by the CG height change and that watershed impervious limits still govern driveways, while Vice Chair Jacobs welcomed the co-living correction. With no public speakers, the hearing remained open 24 hours with a vote scheduled for May 24.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Public hearing held / Vote deferred to May 24

meetings.title: BOCC - May 3, 2021 Work Session Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the six-hour May 3, 2021 work session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners with all five commissioners present. After hearing citizens' comments on the County Manager's 2016 contract, DPS school nurses/social workers, and transit equity, the board reviewed 12 consent agenda items and received extensive briefings on the Community Child Protection/Child Fatality Prevention Teams' 10 recommendations, DFI's market analysis for redeveloping the former DSS Main Street building into affordable Class B/C small-business office and retail space, the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) refresh timeline ahead of a planned 2022 bond referendum, the Triangle's 2027 World University Games bid, and updates on the Durham County Transit Plan scenarios and Triangle Commuter Rail feasibility study. On the sole substantive action item, commissioners voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to approve the City-County Planning Department's FY22 Work Plan (Item 21-0266). During Commissioner Directives and Comments, Chair Howerton and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs clashed over Jacobs's late-night request to add an ARPA funding discussion to the May 10 agenda without agenda-prep review or final U.S. Treasury guidance, before the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Citizens' Comments, and Consent Agenda Review (12 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the work session and read the public charge. Clerk Monica Toomer read emailed comments from Barbara Jacobs urging fiscal restraint on the County Manager's contract and Nicholas Graber-Grace advocating 50 DPS school nurse and social work positions (800+ DAE petition signatures), while Bike Durham's Eric Landfried presented a transit equity rider video. County Manager Wendell Davis then reviewed 12 consent items for the May 10 agenda (including $12.4M IS&T capital modernization, $92.785M Northern High School amendment, FY22 Transit Work Program, and JCPC funding), with Commissioner Nida Allam requesting email follow-up on IT equipment recycling and the northern Durham broadband study.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0232: Community Child Protection Team and Child Fatality Prevention Team Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Kristi Mallett, coordinator Cheryl Scott, DSS Director Ben Rose, Jovetta Whitfield, and Public Health Director Rod Jenkins presented 10 system recommendations: Medicaid expansion (citing maternal/infant mortality and child poverty reductions), universal high-speed broadband (noting gaps in Rougemont), county health coverage for undocumented foster children, implicit bias training, countywide non-Spanish language line access, services for youth with autism and intellectual disabilities, a safe sleep awareness campaign, House Bill 630 / Families First preventive child welfare reform, the Early Childhood Action Plan, and child abuse reporting outreach. Vice Chair Jacobs requested Ms. Scott's Medicaid expansion brief for NCACC advocacy.

agenda_items.title: DFI Update #2: Former DSS Main Street Facility Market Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Director Perry Mann and UNC School of Government DFI Project Manager Sarah Odio presented a market analysis for redeveloping the former DSS Main Street site at East Main and South Roxboro. DFI found roughly 35% of Durham small businesses had closed through February 2021 and downtown Class B/C affordable office space was rapidly disappearing as renovated Class B buildings approached Class A rents (~$38.50/sq ft), while ground-floor retail recovery remained tied to return-to-office trends and 1,500 new downtown households. Next steps include engaging an architect to test Class B/C small-office, retail, artist, lab, and community meeting spaces ahead of August public outreach.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0281: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Refresh Process Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Claudia Hager and financial advisor Doug Carter (DEC Associates) outlined Durham County's ~$600 million existing debt, $225 million upcoming LOBs draw, and >$1 billion 10-year CIP (including >$275 million for DPS), proposing a CIP refresh schedule running from August 2021 facility assessments through February–June 2022 adoption. Vice Chair Jacobs pressed staff to integrate the 2022 GO bond referendum timeline and DPS master facility coordination directly into the schedule, while County Manager Davis and Doug Carter discussed roughly $40 million in remaining 2016 bond funds and Local Government Commission draw-down compliance.

agenda_items.title: Update on Triangle Bid for 2027 World University Games
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andrew Miracle and North Carolina Bid Committee Chair Hill Carrow briefed the board on the Triangle's selection as U.S. candidate city for the 2027 Summer World University Games (FISU), competing internationally ahead of a spring 2022 host decision. Carrow outlined potential Durham venues (Durham County Stadium, Duke, NCCU, Durham Tech), a projected $99 million budget funded largely via national sponsorships, broadcast rights, and state/federal support, and an estimated $150 million regional economic impact.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0266: City-County Planning Department FY22 Work Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Sara Young presented the FY22 Work Plan allocating 46 FTEs across mandated development review and the in-house Comprehensive Plan (including Southeast Durham and Braggtown focus areas), plus minor engineering assistance inspecting GoTriangle bus shelters. Following Vice Chair Jacobs's questions on open space plans, the city's bilingual language access plan, and the new real-time development mapping tool, commissioners voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to adopt the FY22 Work Plan.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Transit Planning Update and Triangle Commuter Rail Feasibility Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation Manager Ellen Beckman and DCHC MPO's Aaron Cain presented three fiscally constrained 20-year transit scenarios ($475M–$500M available beyond committed bus and micro-transit projects): Scenario A (expanded bus frequency, later hours, sidewalks, paratransit), Scenario B (Bus Rapid Transit and dedicated roadway infrastructure), and Scenario C (Commuter Rail to Wake County around 2029). GoTriangle's Jay Heikes then reviewed the Commuter Rail Feasibility Study ($1.8B Durham-to-Garner capital cost, $29M annual operating, five Durham stops, and TJCOG affordable housing and job-access equity analyses). Informational only.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Directives, ARPA/Agenda Process Dispute, Board Training, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff liaison Drew Cummings reported directives were current. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs pushed to add a 15-minute ARPA funding process discussion and the Mayor's vaccine equity proposal to the May 10 agenda, prompting Chair Brenda A. Howerton to rebuke Jacobs for late-night/same-day emails and refuse to add ARPA before agenda-prep review and pending U.S. Treasury guidance (with GM Hager confirming Treasury rules were still awaited). Commissioner Nida Allam proposed initiating board relationship/Coleman Report training below the RFP threshold, and the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) before returning to report staff direction and adjourning.

votes.item_title: Suspend the Rules to Vote on Item 21-0266 (City-County Planning Department FY22 Work Plan)
votes.discussion_detail: Board suspended its work-session rules to take immediate action on the Planning Department's FY22 Work Plan.

votes.item_title: Approve City-County Planning Department FY22 Work Plan (Item 21-0266)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the 46-FTE FY22 Planning Department Work Plan prioritizing the Comprehensive Plan and adding minor GoTriangle bus shelter inspection support.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.discussion_detail: Board entered closed session under attorney-client privilege; upon returning at [06:09:16], Chair Howerton reported direction was given to staff.

disagreements.issue: Process and Timing for Placing ARPA Funding Discussion on the BOCC Agenda
disagreements.summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton and Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs clashed over Jacobs's request to schedule a 15-minute ARPA funding discussion during the May 10 regular session.
disagreements.side_a_position: Place a 15-minute high-level ARPA process discussion on the May 10 regular session agenda (or use commissioner comments time) pursuant to the board's March 22 directive.
side_a_arguments: The March 22 minutes reflected a board directive for Claudia Hager to bring ARPA back at the April/May sessions.
Any three commissioners can request an agenda item, and a 15-minute high-level process discussion required no staff preparation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer ARPA agenda placement to the Chair/Vice Chair agenda-prep meeting until staff prepares materials and U.S. Treasury guidelines are released.
side_b_arguments: Sending emails late Sunday night and mid-day Monday bypassed established agenda-prep procedures and left board members and staff unprepared.
General Manager Claudia Hager advised that the School of Government and State Treasury urged local governments to wait for official U.S. Treasury ARPA guidance before formal discussions.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Howerton declined to place the item on that day's or May 10's agenda without agenda-prep review and moved forward with the agenda.

meetings.title: BOCC - April 26, 2021 Regular Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the April 26, 2021 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved March 8 and March 22 minutes (5-0), adopted ceremonial recognitions for New Hope Audubon Society's Bird-Friendly Durham plan and National Volunteer Week, approved all four consent agenda items 5-0 (including a public art agreement at 318 East Main Street parking deck), received a COVID-19 and vaccine equity update from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins, and announced appointments to the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force (Andrea Hudson) and Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee (Lashelle Welby Jr.). Following a 5-0 vote to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(3), the board returned and unanimously approved a $19,622.25 pre-litigation lease-termination settlement with Neighbors Eatery Restaurant (5-0), then voted 3-2 to authorize Acting County Attorney Willie Darby to finalize an engagement letter with outside attorney Denise Smith Klein to review the County Manager's contract—with Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, and Wendy Jacobs voting Aye and Nimasheena Burns and Brenda A. Howerton voting No after Howerton argued in-house county attorneys could review the contract without spending extra taxpayer funds.

At [00:15:12], Chair Howerton read a proclamation declaring April 18–24, 2021 as National Volunteer Week honoring 300+ volunteers across 40+ county boards and commissions, with Clerk Monica Toomer thanking Tanya de los Santos and Macio Carlton.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (4 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis presented four consent items: Item 239 (designating review officers for the Town of Morrisville), Item 244 (March Property Tax Release and Refund Report), Item 254 (public art agreement with Harrell Salil LLC at the 318 East Main Street parking deck), and Item 257 (NCDOT resolution adding 0.21 miles of Sunstone Drive to the state secondary road system). The board approved all four items 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Health COVID-19 and Vaccine Equity Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 131 active COVID-19 cases, 223 cumulative deaths, and 24,943 total cases, with 43.5% of adults and 73.2% of seniors vaccinated and walk-in clinics open to ages 16+. Commissioners questioned J&J blood-clot precautions, multilingual clinic access, persistent Black and Latinx vaccination gaps (22% Black and 16% Latinx fully vaccinated vs 44% white), and community health worker pay equity.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby announced appointments of Andrea Hudson to the Durham County Safety and Wellness Task Force (with Commissioner Burns serving as county liaison ahead of Wednesday's inaugural meeting) and Lashelle Welby Jr. to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee. disagreements.side_a_position: Engage outside attorney Denise Smith Klein to review the County Manager's contract, conduct separate consultations with each commissioner, and handle related matters.
side_a_arguments: Provides independent legal review and individual consultation with each commissioner on the County Manager's employment contract.
disagreements.side_b_position: Use existing in-house County Attorney staff rather than spending taxpayer funds on outside legal counsel.
side_b_arguments: Durham County already employs competent attorneys capable of interpreting a contract.
Spending taxpayer dollars on outside counsel for a standard contract interpretation is not a good use of county funds or a fair evaluation process.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 3-2 (Ayes: Allam, Carter, Jacobs; Nays: Burns, Howerton).

meetings.title: DCo BOCC April 26 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the April 26, 2021 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (this stream is offset by approximately 39 minutes at the start compared to the alternate broadcast), with all five commissioners present. The board approved March 8 and March 22 minutes 5-0, jointly read a Bird-Friendly Durham resolution and National Volunteer Week proclamation, passed a four-item consent agenda 5-0, reviewed COVID-19 and vaccine equity data with Public Health Director Rod Jenkins, and announced appointments to the Safety and Wellness Task Force and Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee. After entering closed session 5-0 under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(3), the board returned to approve a $19,622.25 pre-litigation settlement with Neighbors Eatery Restaurant 5-0 and passed a 3-2 vote authorizing outside counsel Denise Smith Klein to review the County Manager's contract—with Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, and Wendy Jacobs voting Aye and Nimasheena Burns and Brenda A. Howerton voting No on the grounds that in-house county attorneys should handle contract review.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns reported on DDI Summit and NCACC discussions regarding equitable deployment of federal American Rescue Plan (ARP) tranches across the county, city, and school system. At [00:41:49], the board approved the March 8 and March 22, 2021 regular session minutes 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item 21-0192: Bird-Friendly Durham Resolution and National Volunteer Week Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: All five commissioners took turns reading Resolution 21-0192 endorsing New Hope Audubon Society's Plan and Best Practices for a Bird-Friendly Durham, with New Hope Audubon President Barbara Driscoll thanking the board. At [00:53:23], Chair Howerton read a proclamation declaring April 18–24, 2021 as National Volunteer Week, recognizing 300+ volunteers serving on 40+ boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (4 Items)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis reviewed four consent items: Morrisville review officer designation (239), March property tax release/refund report (244), Harrell Salil LLC public art agreement for 318 East Main Street parking deck (254), and NCDOT secondary road addition for Sunstone Drive (257). The board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Health COVID-19 and Vaccine Equity Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 131 active COVID-19 cases, 223 deaths, and 24,943 cumulative cases, alongside 43.5% adult and 73.2% senior vaccination rates and newly launched walk-in clinic hours. Commissioners discussed J&J vaccine pause lifting, multilingual clinic support, racial vaccination disparities (44% white vs 22% Black and 16% Latinx fully vaccinated), and protecting community health workers from contractor nonpayment.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Acting County Attorney Willie Darby announced the appointments of Andrea Hudson to the Durham County Safety and Wellness Task Force and Lashelle Welby Jr. to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee. At [01:40:54], the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(3).

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Actions: Neighbors Eatery Settlement and Outside Counsel Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning to open session, the board approved a $19,622.25 pre-litigation lease-termination settlement with Neighbors Eatery Restaurant (5-0). meetings.title: April 13, 2021 - Joint City-County Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the April 13, 2021 Joint City-County Committee meeting, attended by BOCC Chair Howerton, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns alongside Mayor Steve Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, and City Council Member DeDreana Freeman. The committee unanimously approved the February 9, 2021 minutes 6-0 on a roll-call vote (BOCC Ayes: Howerton, Jacobs, Burns). Presenters from UNC Gillings and El Centro Hispano detailed the 11-member Back on the Bull Health Ambassador program's outreach to 986 local businesses and ~300 vaccine appointments for essential workers, sparking pointed discussion as Chair Howerton and Council Member Freeman pressed Mayor Schewel to coordinate his informal vaccine-equity stakeholder efforts directly with Public Health Director Rod Jenkins. The committee also reviewed reports on the Durham Small Business Recovery Fund ($1M+ in exhausted grants and $1.15M remaining in 3% unsecured loans, with Chair Howerton and Council Member Freeman requesting race-by-gender breakdowns) and the redesigned 480-participant Durham YouthWorks career-pathways program partnered with Durham Tech.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of February 9, 2021 Joint City-County Committee Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer confirmed a joint quorum comprising Mayor Steve Schewel, Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, BOCC Chair Brenda A. Howerton, Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs, and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns. Council Member Freeman moved approval of the February 9, 2021 minutes, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and the motion passed 6-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: UNC Back on the Bull Health Ambassador Program and Vaccine Equity Coordination
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Kurt Ribisl (UNC), Eliazar Posada (El Centro Hispano), and Dr. Patsy Polston reported that 11 community health ambassadors made 2,700+ visits, enrolled 986 businesses (including ~250 Black- and Latinx-owned businesses), distributed 30,000+ masks, and scheduled nearly 300 vaccine appointments (85% Black or Latinx). Committee members discussed demographic denominators, GIS mapping to avoid duplicating outreach, and Mayor Schewel's informal April 12 meeting with community groups on vaccine equity, with Chair Howerton and Council Member Freeman stressing the need to keep Public Health Director Rod Jenkins central and GM Joanne Pierce calling for explicit focus on structural racism.

agenda_items.title: Durham Small Business Recovery Fund Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Economic Development Officer Andrew Miracle, City OEWD Director Andre Pettigrew, and Carolina Small Business Development Fund CEO Kevin Dick reported that the joint City-County-Duke fund assisted 176 businesses with nearly $1.7 million ($1M+ in exhausted grants at 2/3 minority-owned and >50% women-owned; ~$1.15M remaining in 3% 10-year unsecured loans with 12-month deferral). Dick outlined proposals to rebrand the loan fund, raise the $35,000 cap, and allow refinancing of predatory loans, while Chair Howerton and Council Member Freeman requested disaggregated race-by-gender statistics for Black and Latina women-owned firms.

agenda_items.title: Durham YouthWorks Career Pathways Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City OEWD's Adrienne Graham-Scott, Durham Tech President JB Buxton, Candice Rashada, and Jennifer Fox presented the redesigned four-week hub-and-spoke Durham YouthWorks program serving 480 young adults (ages 16–24 across three 160-person sessions) with $559,500 in city funding and a $75,000 county pledge. By embedding Durham Tech coursework and virtual career simulations aligned with high-growth industries, the program aims to remove transportation and technology barriers, while Vice Chair Jacobs urged connecting youth to Durham College Promise and leveraging county economic incentive agreements for employer placements.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 9, 2021 Joint City-County Committee Minutes
votes.notes: Joint City-County Committee vote: BOCC members Brenda A. Howerton, Wendy Jacobs, and Nimasheena Burns voted Aye alongside City Council members Mayor Steve Schewel, Council Member DeDreana Freeman, and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson for a 6-0 committee tally (BOCC members Nida Allam and Heidi Carter are not on this joint committee).
votes.discussion_detail: Joint City-County Committee approved the February 9, 2021 meeting minutes without edits.

meetings.title: BOCC - April 12, 2021 Regular Session Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the April 12, 2021 regular session of the Durham Board of County Commissioners (the recording begins mid-discussion on Black Maternal Health Week advocacy), with all five commissioners present. The board recognized the Durham County Sheriff's Office for earning full American Correctional Association accreditation (99.7% score), proclaimed April as Child Abuse Prevention Month and Durham County as a Breastfeeding Family Friendly Community, adopted a memorial resolution honoring civil rights and public health pioneer Nathaniel B. White Jr., recognized National County Government Month, and voted 5-0 to adopt Resolution 21-0245 urging state and federal anti-discrimination and hate-crimes legislation ahead of a planned local non-discrimination ordinance. Commissioners also unanimously approved Consent Items 180–238 (5-0)—highlighting a $935,048 City-County interlocal agreement adding 18 staff to expand Bull City United—and received a COVID-19 and vaccine equity briefing from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins before voting 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and adjourning with no action reported.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Discussion: Black Maternal Health Week Advocacy and County Roundtable
agenda_items.discussion_summary: As the recording opens, Vice Chair Jacobs, Chair Howerton, Commissioner Burns, and Commissioner Carter thanked advocates Ms. Lay and Ms. Spencer and the Women's Commission for hosting a weekend Black maternal health forum. Commissioners requested a briefing from GM Joanne Pierce and Public Health staff on existing maternal health services and Lincoln Community Health Center partnerships, and praised Chair Howerton's plan to convene a collaborative community roundtable.

agenda_items.title: Recognition Item 21-0208: Durham County Sheriff's Office ACA Full Accreditation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, Sergeant Cushier, and Lieutenant Hartigan accepted board recognition after the Durham County Detention Facility achieved full American Correctional Association (ACA) accreditation with 100% compliance and a 99.7% audit score—making the Sheriff's Office one of three agencies in North Carolina to hold the national 'Triple Crown' alongside CALEA and medical accreditation.

agenda_items.title: Proclamations: Child Abuse Prevention Month (21-0221) and Breastfeeding Family Friendly Community (21-0224)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jacobs read Proclamation 21-0221 declaring April 2021 as Child Abuse Prevention Month (citing 2,920 suspected reports in FY2019-20), accepted by DSS Director Ben Rose, Assistant Director Jovetta Whitfield, and retiring Program Manager Ann Granby, who discussed House Bill 630 / Families First preventive reforms and Duke racial-disparity research. At [00:34:34], Commissioner Carter read Proclamation 21-0224 recognizing Durham County as a Breastfeeding Family Friendly Community, accepted by Love Anderson of Breastfeed Durham, who highlighted Duke Health's recent decision to drop the RN credential requirement for lactation consultants.

agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolution (21-0240) for Nathaniel B. White Jr. and National County Government Month (21-0241)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns read Memorial Resolution 21-0240 honoring Hillside High School Class of 1963 alumnus, one of Duke University's first five Black undergraduates, and public health statistician/Hayti leader Nathaniel B. White Jr., with tributes from daughter Natalie White and classmates Gloria Rentrope and Walter Jackson. At [00:55:31], Commissioner Nida Allam read Proclamation 21-0241 declaring April 2021 National County Government Month, and GM Deborah Craig-Ray praised Durham County's ~2,000 employees for overcoming the 2020 malware attack and pandemic.

agenda_items.title: Resolution 21-0245: Supporting State and Federal Anti-Discrimination and Hate Crimes Legislation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton read Resolution 21-0245 urging the North Carolina General Assembly to pass the Equality for All Act (HB 50 / S 396) and Hate Crimes Protection legislation and calling on Congress to pass the federal Equality Act (HR 5) and CROWN Act, followed by a statement thanking County Attorney Curtis Massey for legal preparation toward a forthcoming county non-discrimination ordinance. All five commissioners spoke in strong support—citing state anti-transgender bills and county contracting protections—and adopted the resolution 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 180–238)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis presented Consent Items 180–238, previously reviewed during the work session. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs highlighted the $935,048 interlocal agreement with the City of Durham to add 18 staff—outreach workers and violence interrupters—and expand Bull City United into four additional census tracts before the board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 21-0242: Public Health COVID-19 Focus Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following remarks by Commissioner Burns honoring former NCCU Chancellor Edith Wiggins and retiring official Jim Hardin, Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 406 active COVID-19 cases, 221 deaths, and 24,343 cumulative cases, with 89,587 residents (27.9%, including 71.2% of seniors) fully vaccinated and eligibility expanded to Group 5 (16+). Commissioners discussed racial equity heat maps, mobile UNC clinics, Johnson & Johnson allocation, community health worker funding, and Ramadan vaccine guidance for Muslim residents.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton read the statutory basis under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) to discuss real property acquisition or employment contract terms, and the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session. Returning to open session at [02:29:33], Chair Howerton reported directions were given to staff with no action taken, and the board voted 5-0 to adjourn.

votes.discussion_detail: Called on the General Assembly and Congress to pass the Equality for All Act, Hate Crimes Protection Act, federal Equality Act, and CROWN Act, while affirming Durham County's work on a local non-discrimination ordinance.

votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5); returned at [02:29:33] with directions given to staff and no formal action taken.
