meetings.title: BOCC- Regular Session 04-12-21
meetings.executive_summary: At its April 12, 2021 Regular Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened with a moment of silence for victims of community violence, approved prior work session minutes 5-0, and recognized a resolution on the Black Maternal Health Crisis proclaiming April 11-17 as Black Maternal Health Awareness Week. Commissioners also discussed a resolution supporting a local non-discrimination ordinance and state hate crime prevention legislation including the Equality for All Act. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda (Items 180-38, including Bull City United) 5-0 and received a COVID-19 public health and vaccination update from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins. The board concluded by voting 5-0 to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding real property acquisition and employment contract terms, returning with no action taken before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton led the Pledge of Allegiance (with Commissioner Nida Allam reading) and observed a moment of silence for victims of violence across the community and nation. After an announcement regarding Durham-Orange FY22 annual work programs, the board took up the first work session minutes for approval.

agenda_items.title: Resolution on Black Maternal Health Crisis and Black Maternal Health Awareness Week
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns read a resolution developed with the Durham County Women's Commission, Mayor's Council for Women, Equity Before Birth, and MAAME highlighting that Black women accounted for 32.9% of Durham County births in 2018 while Black infants die at more than three times the rate of white infants. Speakers Vivian Slede and Joyce Spencer urged the county to examine its healthcare budget, expand access to midwives, doulas, and prenatal/postpartum care, and build a diverse birth-worker pipeline. Commissioners expressed unanimous support for exploring current county partnerships such as Lincoln Community Health Center and proclaimed April 11-17, 2021 as Black Maternal Health Awareness Week.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Non-Discrimination Ordinance and Hate Crime Prevention Bills
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners spoke in support of a county resolution backing state hate crime prevention legislation, the Equality for All Act, and protections for transgender youth and marginalized residents, while advancing toward a local non-discrimination ordinance. Commissioner Heidi Carter expressed interest in extending explicit non-discrimination protections into Durham County contracts, and Chair Brenda A. Howerton credited County Attorney Curtis Massey and staff for carefully drafting the legal language.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 180 through 38)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented consent agenda items 180 through 38 following prior work session review. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs briefly highlighted and celebrated the Bull City United violence-interruption item without pulling it from consent, and the manager noted a future community presentation on the initiative.

agenda_items.title: Community Recognitions and COVID-19 Public Health & Vaccination Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns recognized recent community passings, centenarian birthdays, and Judge Jim Hardin's retirement after 25 years on the bench. Public Health Director Rod Jenkins then reported 406 active COVID-19 cases and 23,711 cumulative cases, warning against a fourth wave and detailing outreach via UNC mobile clinics, Durham Tech campus vaccinations, geomapping, and community health workers.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Real Property Acquisition and Employment Contract Terms)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted to enter closed session pursuant to G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) to instruct negotiating agents regarding the price and material terms of real property acquisition and employment contract compensation/terms. Upon returning to open session at 02:54:20, the board reported no actions were taken and adjourned.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session - April 5, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: During its April 5, 2021 Work Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners heard emailed citizen comments defending the County Manager's fiscal record and criticizing board tensions, and reviewed 14 consent items including the U.S. Marshals Service detention intergovernmental agreement and a $1.1 million-plus capital amendment for Sheriff's Office body-worn cameras. Commissioners also discussed micro-transit needs for Treyburn, upcoming American Rescue Plan priorities, and a potential animal welfare feral cat ordinance. Procedural disagreements surfaced over the use of open-ended commissioner comments as unscheduled agenda items and over whether board training consultant selection belonged in open or closed session before commissioners reached informal consensus to submit scope-of-work feedback to the attorney by Friday. The board voted 4-0 (with Commissioner Nimasheena Burns temporarily disconnected from the call) to enter closed session on economic development, real property, personnel/contract matters, and attorney-client privilege, returning nearly three hours later to direct staff and adjourn without taking formal action.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge and Emailed Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer read two citizen comments received prior to the deadline (noting one late submission). Larry Crane praised Durham's AAA bond rating and urged renewing the County Manager's contract, while Anthony Jones submitted a letter from the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People criticizing board dysfunction and alleged disrespect toward the county attorney and a potential consultant at the March 8 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Item 180: U.S. Marshals Service and Sheriff's Office Detention Agreement

disagreements.issue: Board Training Consultant Selection Process and Open vs. Closed Session Venue
disagreements.summary: Commissioners disagreed over whether discussions of board training consultants and prior RFP policy handling should occur in open or closed session, as well as the propriety of using open-ended commissioner comments for unscheduled policy topics.
disagreements.side_a_position: Discuss RFP policy context and consultant options openly in public session since no statutory closed-session exception applies to board training, and use commissioner comments to inform the public.
side_a_arguments: County legal guidance indicated there is no North Carolina statutory exception allowing closed session for board training.
Publicly clarifying section 5 of the RFP policy prevents half-truths about prior consultant outreach.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep sensitive personnel/consultant commentary in closed session where appropriate, avoid using open-ended comments as unscheduled agenda items, and establish a formal scope of work for an attorney-led RFP.
side_b_arguments: Open-ended commissioner comment placeholders risk turning unscheduled remarks into de facto agenda items.
Consultant and legal discussions tied to agenda items are more appropriately handled in closed session or through a formal scope-of-work RFP process.
disagreements.resolution: Commissioners agreed by informal consensus at 04:43:50 to submit scope-of-work input for board training to Attorney Darby by Friday so an RFP could be issued.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Session - March 22, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 22, 2021 Regular Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners opened with a Girl Scouts Pledge of Allegiance, added an end-of-agenda discussion on the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, read a board statement condemning anti-minority and anti-Asian hate killings, and approved February 22 minutes 5-0. meetings.title: BOCC Regular Session - March 8, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 8, 2021 Regular Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners approved February minutes with corrections 5-0 and issued ceremonial proclamations for Meals on Wheels Month, National Social Work Month, and Women's History Month. Later, sharp board divisions emerged on two governance votes: first, the board voted 4-1 (Ayes: Nida Allam, Nimasheena Burns, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nay: Brenda A. Howerton) to pursue board training on rules of engagement and managing dissent while directing the County Attorney to bring back two additional consultant proposals alongside the existing 'Bob' group proposal. After a 5-0 vote into closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6), the board returned to open session where Chair Howerton moved—and Commissioner Burns seconded—that Commissioner Carter recuse herself from involvement in the County Manager's contract. Carter refused to recuse herself, and the recusal motion failed 2-3 (Ayes: Brenda A. Howerton, Nimasheena Burns; Nays: Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs) before the board adjourned.

meetings.executive_summary: At its March 1, 2021 Work Session, the Durham Board of County Commissioners reviewed a 16-item consent agenda—including $194,208 for courthouse/detention x-ray machines, $300,000 for 500 East Main Street parking deck architecture, $731,683 for COVID-19 janitorial/facility expenses, and $465,920 for non-congregate homeless housing at Carolina Duke Inn—and voted 5-0 twice to suspend the rules and approve Item 171 (ReCity/Kate's Corner learning centers at three Durham Housing Authority sites). meetings.title: BOCC Budget Retreat - Day 2
meetings.executive_summary: On Day 2 of the Durham Board of County Commissioners FY21-22 Budget Retreat on February 25, 2021, County Manager Wendell Davis and facilitator Martha Marshall opened with a review of Day 1's economic outlook and budget guiding principles. North Carolina Medicaid Chief Administration Officer Melanie Bush briefed the board on Medicaid Transformation to managed care starting July 1, 2021, including Prepaid Health Plans, care management for high-risk pregnancies and children, and non-emergency medical transportation impacts on county DSS staffing. Commissioners then reviewed 52 compiled budget priorities, raising caution over vetting eviction-diversion legal providers ahead of incoming federal stimulus funds, refining priority language (such as Commissioner Nida Allam's tax welfare program correction), and emphasizing small business and entrepreneurship support alongside corporate recruitment. No formal votes were taken during the planning retreat, which concluded with staff preparing for April budget deliberations.

agenda_items.title: Retreat Day 2 Opening and Guiding Principles Framing

disagreements.issue: Delays and Equity in Approving COVID-19 Employee Compensation / Differential Pay
disagreements.summary: Commissioner Nimasheena Burns sharply criticized repeated board delays and questioning over compensating frontline county staff during the pandemic, contrasting that scrutiny with quick approvals for other projects, while colleagues sought FEMA-reimbursement clarity and deferred action to the budget retreat.
disagreements.side_a_position: Move decisively to compensate frontline employees who worked long hours without raises during COVID-19 rather than repeatedly delaying while other projects receive unquestioned funding.
side_a_arguments: Frontline staff worked 12- to 20-hour days without raises for over a year while board members continually asked for more analysis.
Certain county initiatives such as TIF projects and task forces receive funding with minimal scrutiny, making employee compensation an issue of labor equity.
Targeting FEMA 75% reimbursable differential pay rather than the non-reimbursable 5% option is fiscally responsible.
disagreements.side_b_position: Review financial options carefully—including FEMA reimbursement eligibility, liability-free leave alternatives, and broad staff vs. AMI criteria—and defer detailed deliberation to the February 23-24 Budget Retreat.
side_b_arguments: Understanding the difference between differential pay, non-expiring leave liability, and COLA impacts is necessary before adopting a policy.
The board was scheduled to begin a day-and-a-half budget retreat the following morning where full budget trade-offs would be examined.
disagreements.resolution: No vote was taken on February 22; commissioners agreed to carry detailed questions into the February 23-25 Budget Retreat (and subsequently approved 10% FEMA-reimbursable differential pay on March 22).

meetings.title: Joint BOCC-BOE Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton hosted and presided over the joint meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners and the Durham Public Schools Board of Education, opening with a unanimous voice vote approving the November 11, 2020 joint minutes as corrected. Co-chairs Judge Elaine O'Neal and Dr. Cohen presented the proposed Durham City-County Racial Equity Commission bylaws, prompting discussion on youth representation, equal elected-official participation across all three local boards, and budget-retreat timelines for funding stipends. Durham Public Schools administrators then briefed both boards on virtual learning, summer learning legislation in the General Assembly, Northern High School and Lions Farm Elementary capital projects, sustainability standards, and FY 2021-22 budget priorities including HB 90 class-size mandates, $6 million in annual maintenance needs, and staff compensation. During the Pre-K and Durham Head Start update, Chair Howerton and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns raised concerns about last-minute budget requests and emphasized that DPS leadership must coordinate earlier and respect the BOCC chair and budget process ahead of the May 18, 2021 joint meeting.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of November 11, 2020 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton reviewed the joint agenda and opened corrections for the November 11, 2020 minutes. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs requested removing an erroneous 'Doctor' title next to Commissioner Heidi Carter's name. Following the correction, the joint boards approved the minutes by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Durham City-County Racial Equity Commission Bylaws Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Co-chairs Judge Elaine O'Neal and Dr. Cohen discussed proposed bylaws for the Durham City-County Racial Equity Commission, emphasizing robust representation from Durham youth beyond DPS students. Commissioners and board members stressed acting promptly on stipends and budget allocations before upcoming budget retreats and ensuring equal representation of one or two elected officials from the City Council, BOCC, and School Board.

agenda_items.title: DPS Virtual Learning and Summer Learning Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Hardy presented on virtual learning and plans for summer learning programs. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked about federal and state funding for summer learning and safe reopening/staff vaccination, while Superintendent Dr. Mubenga and staff noted a newly filed General Assembly bill prescribing six weeks of summer learning using federal dollars without new state funding; Commissioner Nida Allam also asked about disaggregated demographic data on family preferences for virtual versus in-person instruction.

agenda_items.title: DPS Capital Projects, Sustainability, and MWBE/HUB Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS facilities staff reported construction progress on Northern High School (foundation and arts/cafeteria wing) and Lions Farm Elementary within the $508 million prioritized capital needs from 2019, alongside sustainability design standards. In follow-up remarks, a commissioner urged the boards to budget for dedicated MWBE/HUB expertise rather than treating minority- and women-owned business participation as a checkbox, noting a March session with Tammy Hall on the HUB process.

agenda_items.title: DPS FY 2021-22 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS leadership outlined upcoming FY 2021-22 budget pressures, including stricter HB 90 K-3 class size caps, $6 million needed annually for ongoing maintenance rather than lump-sum capital allocations, counselors and behavioral support staff, and sustaining the $15-per-hour minimum wage ($3.8 million) alongside potential staff raises. Officials also discussed state revenue reserves ($4 billion) and uncollected fines and forfeitures ($750 million statewide), and Board member Lewis asked about the spring digital access study and 1-to-1 IT refresh.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Expansion and Durham Head Start Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Debbie Pittman and Head Start representative Linda reported growth in serving preschoolers with disabilities and Head Start's mixed in-person and virtual delivery launched in January despite tight classroom ratios under COVID-19. In closing remarks, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and Chair Brenda A. Howerton cautioned DPS to submit prioritized funding lists earlier and communicate directly through the BOCC Chair rather than bypassing leadership ahead of the May 18, 2021 joint meeting.

disagreements.issue: 10% Employee Hazard Pay Continuation and Pre-Retreat Cost Visibility
disagreements.summary: Commissioners differed on whether to keep committing funds to the 10% frontline employee hazard pay ahead of the budget retreat without complete multi-item cost totals, versus committing unconditionally to hazard pay for burned-out pandemic staff.
disagreements.side_a_position: Maintain 10% hazard pay unconditionally for frontline workers enduring severe pandemic burnout, supported by strong revenue collections and fund balance growth.
side_a_arguments: County revenue collections and expense management grew the fund balance, leaving the county financially solvent to support hazard pay.
Staff working daily on pandemic programs face severe burnout and put themselves and their families at risk.
Commissioners were elected to make hard choices for the most vulnerable, and no budget retreat will change support for paying workers.
disagreements.side_b_position: Require full cost estimates across proposed start and end dates and weigh all competing funding requests together at the upcoming budget retreat.
side_b_arguments: Budget documents arrived around 5:00 PM just before a 6:00 PM meeting, leaving insufficient time for review.
The board needs a complete picture of total costs to ensure funding is sustainable across all competing county priorities.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; Chair Brenda A. Howerton affirmed appreciation for county staff and deferred detailed budget deliberations to the upcoming board retreat.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session - February 1, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the February 1, 2021 work session with all five commissioners, the county manager, and the county attorney attending. During public comments, the Transit Equity Campaign urged measurable job-access objectives for BIPOC and low-wage riders in the Durham County Transit Plan update, and World Relief Durham requested multi-year county investment to expand bilingual tutoring and mental health services for refugee and immigrant youth. Commissioners then began reviewing the 17-item consent agenda (including a $221,243 WK Dickson stormwater nutrient management contract) and later received ETC Institute's 2020 resident survey showing sharp satisfaction gains in education transparency and strong public support for increased funding in schools (69%) and affordable housing (58%). Following updates on state/federal rental assistance and upcoming Racial Equity Institute and UNC School of Government board trainings, the board voted 5-0 by roll call to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client consultation and adjourned 4-0 after returning with Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs absent.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Public Comments (Transit Equity Campaign and World Relief Durham)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer read an email from Eric Landfried of the Transit Equity Campaign calling on the Durham County Transit Plan update to prioritize BIPOC and low-wage transit riders, set measurable job-access goals (noting a 1-hour transit trip from Oxford Manor to Duke/VA hospitals versus 15 minutes by car), and assume a one-third local county match for commuter rail. Adam Clark of World Relief Durham presented a three-slide funding proposal to close service gaps for refugee and immigrant students beyond the 25% currently served, which Chair Howerton referred to staff.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Items 21-0018 and 21-0028)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis began walking the board through the 17-item consent agenda, including item 21-0018 ($8,540 state DHHS budget amendment) and item 21-0028 ($221,243 contract with WK Dickson for stormwater nutrient management strategy implementation). Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Heidi Carter asked questions regarding neighborhood stakeholder engagement on stormwater projects before the middle portion of the digest truncated.

agenda_items.title: 2020 Durham County Resident Survey Results (ETC Institute)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jason Morado of ETC Institute presented findings from the 2020 Durham County resident survey disaggregated across unincorporated county areas, PAC areas 2–4, and race/ethnicity. Results showed steady overall satisfaction, a steep rise in satisfaction with education-related decision-making transparency (from 23% the prior year), high satisfaction with sheriff protection and public health, and top resident funding priorities in schools (69%) and affordable housing (58%).

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Rental Assistance Updates and Board Governance/Equity Training
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners and staff discussed ongoing federal/state rental assistance distributions (noting roughly $548 million remaining at the state level and newly opened DOT COVID transportation grants) alongside plans for board training. Staff reported ongoing coordination with the Racial Equity Institute (REI) in Greensboro and the UNC School of Government for governance and manager-board alignment sessions for the newly constituted all-female board.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)) and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton read the statutory basis under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with county attorneys under attorney-client privilege. Following a 5-0 roll call vote at 04:32:11 (coupled with a short lunch break until 1:40 PM), the board met in closed session, reconvened at 06:25:33 with Vice Chair Jacobs absent, reported giving direction to staff, and adjourned 4-0.

Howerton presided over the January 25, 2021 regular session with all five commissioners present, opening with a moment of silence for COVID-19 losses and the ceremonial introduction of new EMS Chief Paramedic Mark Lockhart. disagreements.issue: Funding 10% Employee Hazard Pay and Potential Department Budget Cuts (DSS Impact)
disagreements.summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs questioned the fiscal sustainability of funding ongoing 10% hazard pay through lapsed-salary reserves while departments were asked to model budget cuts that could affect DSS assistance, whereas County Manager Wendell Davis and Chair Brenda A. Howerton maintained that hazard pay was covered without threatening DSS funds.
disagreements.side_a_position: Question reliance on April 2020 lapsed-salary strategies for unbudgeted hazard pay until full costs and downstream impacts on mandated DSS programs are clear.
side_a_arguments: Hazard pay was not included in the original April 2020 budget-management blueprint.
Departments are simultaneously being asked to examine conservative budget cuts, which in DSS could threaten mandated rental, emergency, and food assistance.
Commissioners need complete hazard-pay cost totals before making fully informed spending choices.
disagreements.side_b_position: Continue 10% hazard pay using FY 2020 fund balance savings, departmental cash-flow management, and federal reimbursements, with no cuts to DSS assistance.
side_b_arguments: Expenditure mitigation strategies produced $8.9 million in FY 2020 fund balance growth without spending budgeted reserves.
In 30 years of disaster management, federal emergency reimbursements have consistently covered eligible response costs; pressures are isolated to public safety cash-flow timing.
Chair Howerton urged staff to clarify publicly that funding hazard pay will not eliminate any DSS assistance funds.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; County Manager Wendell Davis committed to returning with detailed hazard-pay cost figures and budget clarification.

disagreements.issue: 10% Employee Hazard Pay Funding Sustainability and DSS Budget Impact
disagreements.summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs challenged funding ongoing 10% hazard pay from lapsed-salary reserves while departments faced potential budget reductions, whereas County Manager Wendell Davis and Chair Brenda A. Howerton defended hazard pay funding and rejected suggestions that DSS funds would be cut.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold on committing unbudgeted hazard pay via lapsed-salary reserves until complete cost figures and impacts on other county priorities and DSS are provided.
side_a_arguments: The April 2020 budget-management blueprint did not contemplate hazard pay.
Asking departments to identify conservative budget cuts raises concerns about maintaining DSS assistance and other community needs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain 10% hazard pay backed by $8.9 million in fund balance growth, departmental cash-flow management, and federal disaster reimbursements, without reducing DSS funds.
side_b_arguments: Cost-mitigation strategies generated $8.9 million in FY 2020 fund balance growth without drawing down budgeted reserves.
Federal emergency reimbursements are expected to cover eligible hazard pay costs, with budget pressures limited to public safety cash-flow timing.
Chair Howerton requested explicit public clarification that DSS assistance funds would not be eliminated.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; County Manager Wendell Davis agreed to bring back detailed hazard-pay cost figures and budget clarification.

disagreements.issue: Timing and Retroactivity of $950,000 DPS Classified Staff $15/Hour Pay Funding Ahead of Bond Rating Calls
disagreements.summary: Commissioners and county staff differed over whether to appropriate the full $950,000 for retroactive $15/hour DPS classified employee pay immediately on January 11 or defer action until late January so staff could finalize year-end projections for bond rating agencies.
disagreements.side_a_position: Willingness to take a calculated fiscal risk to act sooner on DPS classified pay and exercise elected policy authority even when differing from cautious staff recommendations.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Heidi Carter argued the disagreement reflected differing 'risk budgets' and supported taking full action on January 11 rather than delaying.

Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs emphasized that elected officials must make decisions aligned with community priorities and values even when differing from staff recommendations, and sought clarity on July 1 versus August 2020 retroactivity.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid rushing financial commitments before delivering accurate year-end fiscal projections to bond rating agencies within three weeks.
side_b_arguments: County staff noted that rating agency calls require accurate, non-speculative year-end outlooks for the current and prior fiscal years.
Deferring the full remaining $950,000 review until January 24/25 allows finance staff to complete projections without rushing rating-agency prep.
disagreements.resolution: Compromise direction reached without a formal vote: move forward at the January 11 meeting with pay retroactive to January 2021 and return later in the month to consider the remaining $950,000 retroactive to August 2020 (subsequently approved on January 25, 2021).

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Session - December 14. 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the December 14, 2020 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, her first regular meeting as Chair with the newly seated 2020–2024 board. The board approved the December 7, 2020 work session minutes (5-0) while pulling the November 23, 2020 regular session minutes for clerk corrections, adopted a ceremonial resolution supporting the NCACC food system resiliency initiative, and made appointments to the Environmental Affairs Board and Homeless Services Advisory Committee. After Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs pulled Item 650 (the 300 East Main Street affordable housing Master Development Agreement) to seek clarification on affordability duration and AMI unit breakdowns, the board unanimously approved pulled consent items 0663 and 0650 (5-0). Following a unanimous closed session on economic development and real property/employment negotiations, the board unanimously approved a $50,000 vacant property purchase (PINs 171556, 171557, and 171558) and a 10-year restaurant lease in Suite 150 at 201 East Main Street before adjourning.

meetings.title: Durham County Government BOCC Live
meetings.executive_summary: This livestream recording captures the December 14, 2020 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners presided over by Chair Brenda A. Howerton. The board unanimously approved the December 7, 2020 work session minutes (5-0), adopted a food system resiliency resolution for NCACC, and voted 5-0 on an amended motion by Commissioner Nimasheena Burns to allocate $124,000 from the remaining $819,000 BOCC COVID Relief Fund balance to continue Hope Learning Centers through January while deferring broader fall funding questions to a January work session. After Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs pulled Item 650 (300 East Main Street Master Development Agreement) over affordability duration and AMI unit-mix questions—prompting brief pushback over pulling an item staff said needed action that night—the board unanimously approved pulled consent items 0663 and 0650 (5-0). Following closed session, the board unanimously approved a $50,000 vacant property purchase (PINs 171556, 171557, and 171558) and a 10-year restaurant lease at 201 East Main Street (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Pledge of Allegiance, Chair Remarks, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Nida Allam led the Pledge of Allegiance, and Chair Brenda A. Howerton thanked her colleagues for electing her board chair. Chair Howerton read announcements including Mount Vernon Baptist Church's December 17 free produce distribution and Welcome Baby's upcoming January coat drive.

agenda_items.title: Approval of December 7, 2020 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton held the November 23 regular session minutes for clerk follow-up and called for a motion on the December 7 work session minutes. The board approved the December 7 minutes 5-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer read one public comment raising concerns over whether CARES Act spending authorized by County Manager Davis in March was fully federally reimbursed and questioning why it was not presented in the budget.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution Supporting NCACC Food System Resiliency Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton read a resolution prepared with Deborah Craig-Ray endorsing the NCACC presidential initiative and task force on food system resiliency. All five commissioners were to sign the resolution for forwarding to the association.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Overview and Pull of Item 650
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager summarized consent items including utility contracts, a $1,178,584.02 Microsoft Enterprise Agreement, Snow Hill lift station testing, and 300 East Main Street contracts and $20.8 million limited obligation bond funding (Item 653). Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked to pull Item 650 (300 East Main Street Master Development Plan/Agreement) to the end of the agenda for review, leading to a brief exchange over whether her concerns could still be voted on that night to meet project deadlines.

agenda_items.title: Hope Learning Centers Continuation Funding ($124,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following presentations from three learning center providers, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns moved—and amended with Vice Chair Jacobs and finance staff input—to approve $124,000 in continuation funding through the end of January for Hope Learning Centers from the $819,000 remaining balance in the BOCC COVID Relief Fund. Commissioner Heidi Carter emphasized the urgency of supporting students struggling with remote learning while deferring broader fall funding questions to the January work session.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler began the boards and commissions appointment results, starting with one vacant seat on the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Items 0650 and 0663 (300 East Main Street Affordability & Shelter Funding)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jacobs questioned how the 300 East Main Street Master Development Agreement secures affordability in perpetuity and reflects the specific 30% and 50% AMI unit mix rather than only an 80% AMI cap. Staff explained ground lease renegotiation and reversion protections as well as Urban Ministries / Marriott shelter funding from the $1.01 million July allocation before the board approved Items 0663 and 0650 unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Post-Closed Session Real Estate Actions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session on economic development incentives, real property acquisition, and employment contract terms. Returning to open session at 03:51:07, the board reported giving staff economic development direction and voted 5-0 to purchase three vacant parcels (PINs 171556, 171557, and 171558) for $50,000 and 5-0 to approve a 10-year restaurant lease in Suite 150 at 201 East Main Street.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Newly elected Board of County Commissioners Chair Brenda A. Howerton presided over the December 9, 2020 Joint City-County Committee meeting alongside Durham Mayor Steve Schewel and City Council and BOCC members, honoring Mary Ann Black as the only prior African American woman to chair the BOCC. The committee received informational briefings on COVID-19 positivity (5.1%) and vaccine rollout transparency from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins, year-round food security initiatives, and joint small-business relief—where $1 million in grants and $577,000 in loans had been awarded and $240,000 in Durham CARES grants were advancing ahead of the December 30 federal deadline. Officials also reviewed Hope Learning Centers funding needs for approximately 300 vulnerable students, round-two ESG COVID homeless shelter and White Flag winter operations (including whether ESG restrictions permitted hotel acquisition), and foster care / emergency rental assistance challenges before adjourning without formal votes.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks, Agenda Time Management, and Welcome to New BOCC Leadership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton opened the joint committee meeting and set a 15-minute-per-report schedule to adjourn on time. Mayor Steve Schewel congratulated Chair Howerton and the newly seated county commissioners, and Howerton reflected on serving as only the second African American female BOCC chair after Mary Ann Black.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update and Vaccine Rollout Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported a 5.1% lab positivity rate and noted that outreach with El Centro Hispano, LATIN-19, and Spanish-language radio had reduced Latinx cases from 78% of new infections in early summer, while inequities persisted. Answering Council Member Johnson, Jenkins described surveys of public health, EMS, police, and fire staff for vaccine readiness and plans for community town halls on vaccine transparency.

agenda_items.title: Food Security and Eat and See Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presenter Donna reviewed partnerships with farmers markets, PPE and volunteer support for food pantries, the county-funded year-round Food Security Coordinator position, and adjustments to Eat and See family meal delivery. Chair Howerton noted that food insecurity was also an NCACC presidential priority she planned to bring forward via resolution.

agenda_items.title: Small Business Grant and Loan Fund & Durham CARES Grants Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Office of Economic and Workforce Development Director Andre Pettigrew reported that the joint $1 million small business grant program was fully awarded and the $2 million long-term (9-year, 3% interest) loan fund had lent $577,000 to 25 businesses, leaving ~$1.2 million available. He also outlined the new Durham CARES Small Business Grant program ($240,000 already awarded by the City, with County action pending before the December 30 CARES Act deadline) and addressed duplication-of-benefits tracking.

agenda_items.title: Hope Learning Centers and Digital Equity Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Megan and Dr. Harding presented an update on Hope Learning Centers serving roughly 300 vulnerable students with digital equity and remote-learning support. Commissioners noted the ongoing funding gap as initial funds expire and scheduled deeper review at the upcoming BOCC meeting.

agenda_items.title: ESG COVID Funds, Homeless Shelter Operations, and White Flag Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated the committee on Round 1 ESG COVID funds supporting Urban Ministries at Liberty Street and Carolina Duke Inn, over $2 million in Round 2 city ESG funds, a White Flag winter shelter program targeted for January 1, and $783,633 in competitive state ESG funds due January 22. Responding to Mayor Schewel on using ESG money to purchase a hotel instead of paying high nightly room rates, staff explained that federal ESG strings require a purchased hotel to operate solely as an emergency shelter for 3 to 10 years without covering ongoing operating costs.

agenda_items.title: Housing, Emergency Assistance, Child Welfare, and Diversion Programs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Department of Social Services and county staff reviewed high-volume emergency housing assistance applications, public-private partnership planning, challenges placing COVID-positive children in foster care, and diversion programs.

agenda_items.title: HB2 Discussion and Next Joint Meeting Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton reported contacting Kevin Leonard at the NCACC regarding HB2 so city and county positions stay coordinated, announced the next joint committee meeting for February 9 at 9:00 a.m., and adjourned the session.

meetings.title: Durham County Government BOCC Live WorkSession Dec 7 2020
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 7, 2020 organizational work session, Durham County Board of Elections Chair Phil Lehman certified the 2020 election results for the five seated commissioners and reported historic turnout of roughly 180,000 voters (74% of registered voters). Presided over initially by County Attorney Lowell Siler, the board unanimously elected Brenda A. Howerton as Chair (5-0), but split 2-3 on Chair Howerton's nomination of Nimasheena Burns for Vice Chair—Ayes: Nimasheena Burns and Brenda A. Howerton; Nays: Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Wendy Jacobs—before Wendy Jacobs was elected Vice Chair in the subsequent omitted ballot. Chair Howerton requested January board-manager relations and Racial Equity Institute (REI) trainings in response to an investigation involving former commissioners, and the board unanimously voted 5-0 to suspend the rules, approve the public officials bond (5-0), and adopt the 2021 meeting schedule as amended to avoid a September 7 Rosh Hashanah conflict (5-0).

agenda_items.title: 2020 Election Certification Report by Board of Elections Chair Phil Lehman
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board of Elections Chair Phil Lehman reported that roughly 180,000 Durham residents voted in the November 2020 election—118,000 during early voting, 47,000 by mail, and only ~14,000 (8%) on Election Day—representing 74% turnout compared to 68% in 2016. Lehman praised Director Derek Bowens, staff, and poll volunteers for maintaining smooth operations with backup generators during power outages and minimal changes during recounts.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair (Brenda A. Howerton)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler opened nominations for Board Chair, and Brenda A. Howerton was nominated. By roll-call voice vote, the board unanimously elected Howerton as Chair (5-0), after which Howerton outlined priorities including the NCACC '100 Counties, Our Children' initiative and fiscal efficiency during the pandemic downturn.

agenda_items.title: Election of Vice Chair (Failed Nomination of Nimasheena Burns; Wendy Jacobs Seated as Vice Chair)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton cited community calls for racial equity and Black and brown women's leadership in nominating Commissioner Nimasheena Burns for Vice Chair. Burns and Howerton voted Aye while Commissioners Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Wendy Jacobs voted No, failing 2-3 for lack of the three-vote majority; in the subsequent turn (following a transcript gap), Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs thanked colleagues for electing her Vice Chair and delivered her third-term priorities address.

agenda_items.title: Chair Request for Board-Manager Relations and Racial Equity Institute Training
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Howerton announced that to address issues emerging from an investigation involving former commissioners and strengthen board relationships, she was asking the County Manager and County Attorney to schedule manager-commissioner relations training and Racial Equity Institute (REI) training for early January.

agenda_items.title: Suspension of Rules and Approval of Public Officials Bond
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon guidance from County Attorney Siler, Commissioner Heidi Carter moved to suspend the rules so the board could vote during the work session, which passed 5-0. The board then approved the public officials bond 5-0 on Carter's motion.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2021 BOCC Meeting Schedule (Amended for Rosh Hashanah Conflict)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs noted that moving the September 2021 work session to Tuesday, September 7 due to Labor Day created a conflict with Rosh Hashanah. The board voted 5-0 to approve the 2021 meeting schedule as amended excluding the September 7 date.

votes.notes: Siler called each member by name and announced unanimous selection of Brenda A. Howerton as Chair.
votes.discussion_detail: County Attorney Lowell Siler presided over the election of Chair Howerton with no competing nominations.

votes.discussion_detail: Chair Howerton nominated Commissioner Burns citing racial equity and community emails; County Attorney Siler noted three votes are required and no second is needed for a nomination.

votes.notes: Commissioner Allam appears as 'Commissioner Long' in ASR.

votes.notes: Initially moved at 00:37:07 prior to rules suspension, then re-voted after rules were suspended.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the statutory public officials bond for incoming/seated county officials.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not identified by name in the audio transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the 2021 BOCC meeting schedule except for the September work session date, which conflicted with Rosh Hashanah on Tuesday, September 7.

disagreements.issue: Selection of BOCC Vice Chair (Nimasheena Burns Nomination vs. Wendy Jacobs)
disagreements.summary: Following Brenda A. Howerton's unanimous election as Chair, the board split 2-3 on Howerton's nomination of newly seated Commissioner Nimasheena Burns for Vice Chair before Wendy Jacobs was elected Vice Chair.
disagreements.side_a_position: Elevate newly elected Commissioner Nimasheena Burns to Vice Chair in recognition of racial equity and community calls for Black and brown women's leadership.
side_a_arguments: Chair Brenda A. Howerton cited numerous community emails and the national/local context of Black and brown women's leadership in putting forward Burns's name.
disagreements.side_b_position: Decline to support Burns's nomination for Vice Chair and instead support third-term Commissioner Wendy Jacobs.
side_b_arguments: Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Wendy Jacobs voted No on Burns's nomination without extended floor debate, leaving Burns one vote short of the required three-vote majority.
disagreements.resolution: Burns's nomination failed 2-3; Wendy Jacobs was subsequently elected Vice Chair.

disagreements.summary: The newly seated board divided 2-3 against Chair Brenda A. Howerton's nomination of Nimasheena Burns for Vice Chair and then elected Wendy Jacobs 3-2.
disagreements.side_a_position: Elect newly seated Commissioner Nimasheena Burns as Vice Chair to reflect racial equity and community advocacy for Black and brown women's leadership.
side_a_arguments: Chair Howerton cited extensive community emails and racial equity considerations in nominating Burns.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject Burns's nomination and elect veteran Commissioner Wendy Jacobs as Vice Chair.
side_b_arguments: Heidi Carter, Nida Allam, and Wendy Jacobs voted No on Burns's nomination; Allam and Jacobs are recorded voting Aye on the 3-2 ballot electing Jacobs (with Howerton voting Nay and Carter/Burns split in the unrecorded gap).
disagreements.resolution: Wendy Jacobs was elected Vice Chair on a 3-2 vote.

meetings.search_blob: bocc work session - december 7, 2020 brenda a. howerton this recording of the december 7, 2020 bocc organizational work session begins with board of elections chair phil lehman certifying the election of nida allam, nimasheena burns, heidi carter, brenda a. howerton, and wendy jacobs amid historic 74% turnout (~180,000 voters). the board unanimously elected brenda a. howerton as chair (5-0), then split on two vice chair ballots: chair howerton's nomination of nimasheena burns failed 2-3 (ayes: nimasheena burns, brenda a. howerton; nays: heidi carter, nida allam, wendy jacobs), after which wendy jacobs was elected vice chair 3-2 (nida allam and wendy jacobs recorded aye, brenda a. howerton recorded nay, with carter and burns splitting the remaining two votes in the preceding omitted segment). chair howerton also called for january manager-commissioner relations and racial equity institute trainings, and the board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules, approve the public officials bond (5-0), and adopt the 2021 meeting schedule excluding a september 7 rosh hashanah conflict (5-0). governance & transparency certification of 2020 bocc election results by board of elections chair phil lehman election of board chair (brenda a. howerton) election of vice chair (split votes: burns failed 2-3; jacobs elected 3-2) chair directives on board-manager relations and racial equity institute training suspension of rules and approval of public officials bond approval of 2021 bocc meeting schedule (amended) election of brenda a. howerton as chair of the board of county commissioners election of vice chair — nomination of nimasheena burns election of vice chair — election of wendy jacobs motion to suspend the rules to vote during work session approval of public officials bond approval of 2021 bocc meeting schedule (amended to exclude september 7) selection of bocc vice chair (nimasheena burns nomination vs. wendy jacobs election)
